title.zh: 卷七十 鄭孔荀列傳
title.en: Volume 70: Biographies of Zheng, Kong, Xun
title.raw: 卷七十 鄭孔荀列傳 Volume 70: Biographies of Zheng, Kong, Xun

sentences.zh: 鄭太

translations.literal: Zheng Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tai.

sentences.zh: 〈（即鄭泰）〉

translations.literal: (That is, Zheng Tai.) Closing bracket.〉
translations.idiomatic: The text identifies him as Zheng Tai; the commentary closes.〉

sentences.zh: 孔融 荀彧

translations.literal: Kong Rong. Xun Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong; Xun Yu.

sentences.zh: 鄭太字公業，河南開封人，司農衆之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Zheng Tai, courtesy name Gongye, was a native of Kaifeng in Henan, and was the great-grandson of Minister of Agriculture Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tai, styled Gongye, came from Kaifeng in Henan; he was a fourth-generation descendant of Zheng Zhong, the minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 〈開封，縣，故城在今汴州南。〉

translations.literal: Kaifeng is a county; its old walled town is south of present Bianzhou.〉
translations.idiomatic: Note: Kaifeng was a county; its old city lay south of what is now Kaifeng in Henan.〉

sentences.zh: 少有才略。

translations.literal: In youth he had talent and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: From his youth he showed ability and strategic sense.

sentences.zh: 靈帝末，知天下將亂，陰交結豪桀。

translations.literal: Near the end of Emperor Ling, knowing the realm would be thrown into chaos, he secretly associated with heroic men.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Ling's reign, foreseeing turmoil, he secretly befriended bold men of action.

sentences.zh: 家富於財，有田四百頃，而食常不足，名聞山東。

translations.literal: His family was rich in wealth, had four hundred qing of fields, yet food was often insufficient; his name was heard east of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: His clan was wealthy and held four hundred qing of land, yet he spent so freely that he often ran short; his generosity made his name known throughout the northeast.

sentences.zh: 初舉孝廉，三府辟，公車徵，皆不就。

translations.literal: At first he was recommended as filial and incorrupt; the three offices summoned him; the public carriage summoned him; all he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was nominated as filial and incorrupt, received summons from the three high offices and from the imperial coach, and declined every offer.

sentences.zh: 及大將軍何進輔政，徵用名士，以公業爲尚書侍郎，

translations.literal: When Grand General He Jin assisted government, he summoned and employed famous scholars, and made Gongye secretary attendant of the secretariat,
translations.idiomatic: When Grand General He Jin took charge of the government and recruited eminent men, he named Zheng Gongye secretary attendant of the secretariat,

sentences.zh: 〈續漢志曰：「尚書凡六曹，侍郎三十六人，四百石。

translations.literal: 〈The Continued Han Treatise says: The secretariat in all has six bureaus; attendants are thirty-six persons, four hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Continued Han Treatise states: "the secretariat had six bureaus, thirty-six attendant posts at four hundred bushels salary,

sentences.zh: 一曹有六人，主作文書起草。」〉

translations.literal: each bureau has six persons, in charge of composing documents and drafting.〉
translations.idiomatic: six men to each bureau, charged with drafting documents and memorials."〉

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 進將誅閹官，欲召并州牧董卓爲助。

translations.literal: Jin was about to execute the palace officials and wished to summon Bingzhou governor Dong Zhuo as aid.
translations.idiomatic: When He Jin prepared to purge the eunuchs, he meant to summon Dong Zhuo, governor of Bingzhou, as an ally.

sentences.zh: 公業謂進曰：「董卓彊忍寡義，志欲無猒。

translations.literal: Gongye said to Jin: Dong Zhuo is forcible, cruel, and scant in righteousness; his aims and desires know no satiety.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Gongye warned He Jin: "Dong Zhuo is ruthless, treacherous, and insatiable;

sentences.zh: 若借之朝政，

translations.literal: If you lend him a role in court government,
translations.idiomatic: if you give him a hand in governing,

sentences.zh: 〈借音子夜反。〉

translations.literal: 〈Borrow is read with the ziye fan pronunciation.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Comment: the character glossed as borrow is read with the ziye fan spelling (zye plus ye).〉

sentences.zh: 授以大事，將恣凶慾，必危朝廷。

translations.literal: entrust him with great affairs, he will give free rein to fierce desires, and will certainly endanger the court.
translations.idiomatic: Hand him great power, and he will indulge his violent appetites and endanger the throne.

sentences.zh: 明公以親德之重，據阿衡之權，秉意獨斷，誅除有罪，誠不宜假卓以爲資援也。

translations.literal: My lord, by the weight of close virtue, grasping the power of Yi Yin, holding intent and deciding alone, executing and removing the guilty, truly ought not lend Zhuo as a supporting resource.
translations.idiomatic: You stand near the throne with the authority of a Yi Yin; you need only act decisively and execute the guilty—you should not make Dong Zhuo your prop.

sentences.zh: 且事留變生，殷鑒不遠。」

translations.literal: Moreover if the affair is delayed change will arise; the Yin mirror is not far.
translations.idiomatic: Delay invites treachery, and the lesson of Yin is still before our eyes."

sentences.zh: 又爲陳時務之所急數事。

translations.literal: He also for him set forth several matters urgent in current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to list several pressing points of policy.

sentences.zh: 進不能用，乃弃官去。

translations.literal: Jin could not use it; then he abandoned office and left.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin ignored him; Zheng Tai resigned his post and left.

sentences.zh: 謂潁川人荀攸曰：「何公未易輔也。」

translations.literal: He said to Xun You of Yingchuan: Lord He is not easy to assist.
translations.idiomatic: He told Xun You of Yingchuan, "Lord He will not be easy to serve."

sentences.zh: 進尋見害，卓果作亂。

translations.literal: Jin soon was harmed; Zhuo indeed raised chaos.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin was killed soon after, and Dong Zhuo did exactly as Zheng Tai had feared.

sentences.zh: 公業等與侍中伍瓊、卓長史何顒共說卓，以袁紹爲勃海太守，以發山東之謀。

translations.literal: Gongye and others together with palace attendant Wu Qiong and Zhuo's chief clerk He Yong jointly persuaded Zhuo to appoint Yuan Shao governor of Bohai, in order to set off the plot east of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tai, with Palace Attendant Wu Qiong and Dong Zhuo's chief clerk He Yong, persuaded Dong Zhuo to name Yuan Shao governor of Bohai and so trigger the coalition east of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 及義兵起，卓乃會公卿議，大發卒討之，羣僚莫敢忤旨。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, Zhuo then convened dukes and ministers to deliberate, greatly raised soldiers to attack them; the host of officials none dared oppose the decree.
translations.idiomatic: When the coalition rose, Dong Zhuo called the high ministers together, levied a great host to crush it, and no one dared gainsay him.

sentences.zh: 公業恐其衆多益橫，凶彊難制，獨曰：「夫政在德，不在衆也。」

translations.literal: Gongye feared that if their numbers grew they would become more overbearing, fierce and strong and hard to control; alone he said: Government lies in virtue, not in numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Gongye feared that if their numbers grew they would become more overbearing, fierce and strong and hard to control; alone he said: "Government lies in virtue, not in numbers."

sentences.zh: 卓不恱，曰，「如卿此言，兵爲無用邪？」

translations.literal: Zhuo was not pleased and said, If according to your words this is so, are troops useless?
translations.idiomatic: "Zhuo was not pleased and said, If according to your words this is so, are troops useless?"

sentences.zh: 公業懼，乃詭詞更對曰：

translations.literal: Gongye feared; then with deceitful words he again replied, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tai grew alarmed and answered evasively,

sentences.zh: 〈詭猶詐也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Deceitful means fraudulent.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Comment: here the word rendered deceitful means fraudulent.〉

sentences.zh: 非謂無用，以爲山東不足加大兵耳。

translations.literal: It is not that I mean useless; I consider that east of the mountains does not warrant adding great troops.
translations.idiomatic: Not that arms are useless—I mean the east does not warrant a major campaign.

sentences.zh: 如有不信，試爲明公略陳其要。

translations.literal: If there is disbelief, I will try for my lord briefly to set forth the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: If you doubt me, let me sketch the main reasons for my lord.

sentences.zh: 今山東合謀，州郡連結，人庶相動，非不強盛。

translations.literal: Now east of the mountains they combine in plot; commanderies and prefectures link together; the people stir one another; it is not that they are not strong and flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: The coalition east of the mountains has linked commandery with commandery and roused the common people—they are not weak.

sentences.zh: 然光武以來，中國無警，百姓優逸，忘戰日乆。

translations.literal: Yet since Emperor Guangwu, within China there has been no alarm; the hundred surnames have been leisurely and easy; they have forgotten war for a long day.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since Emperor Guangwu the heartland has known no war; the people have lived at ease and forgotten how to fight.

sentences.zh: 仲尼有言：『不敎人戰，是謂弃之。』

translations.literal: Confucius had a saying: Not teaching men to fight is called abandoning them.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "To send untrained men into battle is to throw them away."

sentences.zh: 其衆雖多，不能爲害。

translations.literal: Though their host is numerous, it cannot do harm.
translations.idiomatic: Their numbers therefore cannot truly harm you.

sentences.zh: 一也。

translations.literal: This is one.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first point.

sentences.zh: 明公出自西州，少爲國將，閑習軍事，數踐戰埸，名振當世，人懷懾服。

translations.literal: My lord came from the western provinces; in youth you were a general of the state, practiced in military affairs, repeatedly trod the battlefield; your name shook the age; people harbor awe and submission.
translations.idiomatic: You hail from the northwest, have been a general since youth, know war from experience, and your name alone overawes the age—that is the second point.

sentences.zh: 二也。

translations.literal: This is two.
translations.idiomatic: Second point.

sentences.zh: 袁本初公卿子弟，生處京師。

translations.literal: Yuan Benchu is a son of dukes and ministers, born and living in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao is a son of the great families of Luoyang—

sentences.zh: 張孟卓東平長者，

translations.literal: Zhang Mengzhuo is an elder worthy of Dongping,
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Miao of Dongping is a respectable elder—

sentences.zh: 〈孟卓名邈。〉

translations.literal: Mengzhuo's given name is Miao.〉
translations.idiomatic: Note: Mengzhuo is Zhang Miao.〉

sentences.zh: 坐不闚堂。

translations.literal: sits without peeping into the hall.
translations.idiomatic: He is the sort of man proverbially said never to glance beyond his own hall.

sentences.zh: 〈言不妄視也。〉

translations.literal: 〈It means he does not rashly look about.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The phrase means he does not look rashly about.〉

sentences.zh: 孔公緒

translations.literal: Kong Gongxu
translations.idiomatic: Kong Zhou

sentences.zh: 〈名伷。〉

translations.literal: His given name is Zhou.〉
translations.idiomatic: Note: his given name was Zhou.〉

sentences.zh: 清談高論，噓枯吹生。

translations.literal: pure talk and lofty discourse, blowing withered to life and blowing the living to withered.
translations.idiomatic: He is a man of lofty talk who can make the dead seem alive and the living seem dead.

sentences.zh: 〈枯者噓之使生，生者吹之使枯。

translations.literal: 〈The withered he breathes on to make live; the living he blows on to make withered.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The commentary glosses: he breathes life into the withered and blows vitality from the living—

sentences.zh: 言談論有所抑揚也。〉

translations.literal: It means in talk and discourse there is praise and blame.〉
translations.idiomatic: that is, his conversation exaggerates and deprecates at will.〉

sentences.zh: 並無軍旅之才，埶銳之幹，臨鋒決敵，非公之儔。

translations.literal: Together they lack talent for armies and hosts, keen edge of capability; facing the blade and deciding the enemy, they are not a match for my lord.
translations.idiomatic: None of them has military talent or the edge to meet you blade to blade—they are not in your class. That is the third point.

sentences.zh: 三也。

translations.literal: This is three.
translations.idiomatic: Third point.

sentences.zh: 山東之士，素乏精悍。

translations.literal: Gentlemen east of the mountains have always lacked keen bravery.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry of the northeast have never been known for toughness—

sentences.zh: 〈悍，勇也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Keen means brave.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Comment: here the word rendered keen means brave.〉

sentences.zh: 未有孟賁之勇，慶忌之捷，

translations.literal: they have not the courage of Meng Ben nor the agility of Qing Ji,
translations.idiomatic: They have neither the raw strength of Meng Ben nor the speed of Qing Ji.

sentences.zh: 〈說菀曰：「孟賁水行不避鮫龍，陸行不避虎狼，發怒吐氣，聲響動天。」

translations.literal: 〈The Garden of Persuasions says: Meng Ben in water travel did not avoid sharks and dragons; on land travel did not avoid tigers and wolves; when angry he spat breath and sound shook heaven."
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Garden of Persuasions says: Meng Ben in water travel did not avoid sharks and dragons; on land travel did not avoid tigers and wolves; when angry he spat breath and sound shook heaven."

sentences.zh: 許慎注《淮南子》曰：「孟賁，衞人也。」

translations.literal: Xu Shen's commentary on the Huainanzi says: Meng Ben was a man of Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shen's commentary on the Huainanzi says: Meng Ben was a man of Wei."

sentences.zh: 《呂氏春秋》曰：「 孟賁過於河，先其伍，船人怒，以楫虓其頭，不知其孟賁故也。

translations.literal: The Lüshi Chunqiu says: Meng Ben crossed a river ahead of his squad; the boatman in anger used an oar to strike his head, not knowing he was Meng Ben for that reason.
translations.idiomatic: The Lüshi Chunqiu says: "Meng Ben crossed a river ahead of his squad; the boatman in anger used an oar to strike his head, not knowing he was Meng Ben for that reason.

sentences.zh: 中河，孟賁瞋目視船人，髮植目裂，舟中人盡播入河。」

translations.literal: Mid-river, Meng Ben glared at the boatman; hair stood upright and eyes split; everyone in the boat was shaken into the river."
translations.idiomatic: midstream Meng Ben glared until his hair bristled and his eyes seemed to tear; the whole boatload tumbled into the water—"

sentences.zh: 慶忌，吳王僚子也。

translations.literal: Qing Ji was the son of King Liao of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Ji was a son of King Liao of Wu—

sentences.zh: 射之矢，滿把不能中，四馬追之不能及。〉

translations.literal: Arrows shot at him filled a handful yet could not hit; four horses pursued him yet could not catch up.〉
translations.idiomatic: arrows filled his grip yet could not strike him, and four-horse teams could not overtake him.〉

sentences.zh: 聊城之守，

translations.literal: the defense of Liaocheng,
translations.idiomatic: They cannot match the stubborn defense of Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 〈《史記》，燕將攻下聊城，因保守之。

translations.literal: 〈The Records says: a Yan general captured Liaocheng and therefore held and defended it.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Records tells how a Yan general took Liaocheng and held it—

sentences.zh: 齊將田單攻之，歲餘不下。〉

translations.literal: The Qi general Tian Dan attacked it; more than a year he could not take it.〉
translations.idiomatic: while Tian Dan of Qi besieged it for over a year without success.〉

sentences.zh: 良、平之謀，可任以偏師，責以成功。

translations.literal: the stratagems of Liang and Ping—one may entrust them with a detached column and charge them with success.
translations.idiomatic: They are no Zhang Liang or Chen Ping: you could send a single column and expect victory. That is the fourth point.

sentences.zh: 四也。

translations.literal: This is four.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth point.

sentences.zh: 就有其人，而尊卑無序，王爵不加，若恃衆怙力，

translations.literal: Suppose there were such men, yet noble and base lack order, royal enfeoffment is not applied; if they rely on numbers and trust in force,
translations.idiomatic: Even if such men existed, the coalition has no clear chain of command and no royal commission; if they lean on numbers and brute strength—

sentences.zh: 〈怙亦恃也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Trust also means rely on.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Comment: the word rendered trust also means rely on.〉

sentences.zh: 將各基峙，

translations.literal: the generals will each base themselves and stand apart,
translations.idiomatic: Each general will dig in on his own ground.

sentences.zh: 〈峙，止也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Stand apart means stop.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Comment: the word rendered stand apart means halt or stand firm.〉

sentences.zh: 以觀成敗，不肯同心共膽，與齊進退。

translations.literal: to watch success or failure, unwilling to share one heart and one gall, advance and retreat with Qi together.
translations.idiomatic: They would watch how the fight goes and refuse to risk life and fortune together. That is the fifth point.

sentences.zh: 五也。

translations.literal: This is five.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth point.

sentences.zh: 關西諸郡，頗習兵事，自頃以來，數與羌戰，婦女猶戴戟操矛，挾弓負矢，

translations.literal: The various commanderies west of the pass are rather practiced in military affairs; in recent times they have repeatedly fought the Qiang; women still wear halberds and grasp spears, hold bows and bear arrows,
translations.idiomatic: The northwestern commanderies are war-hardened; for years they have fought the Qiang—even women carry halberds, spears, bows, and quivers—

sentences.zh: 〈挾，持也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Hold means grasp.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Comment: the word rendered hold means grasp.〉

sentences.zh: 況其壯勇之士，以當妄戰之人乎！

translations.literal: how much more their stalwart brave gentlemen, to oppose men who fight rashly!
translations.idiomatic: Think how much more their fighting men will prevail against these untrained levies!

sentences.zh: 其勝可必。

translations.literal: Their victory can be certain.
translations.idiomatic: Victory is assured.

sentences.zh: 六也。

translations.literal: This is six.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth point.

sentences.zh: 且天下彊勇，百姓所畏者，有并、涼之人，及匈奴、屠各、湟中義從、西羌八種，

translations.literal: Moreover the realm's strong and brave, whom the hundred surnames fear, include the men of Bing and Liang, and the Xiongnu, Tuge, Huangzhong volunteer followers, and the eight kinds of western Qiang,
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the fiercest fighters in the empire—the very names that terrify the people—are the men of Bing and Liang, the Xiongnu, the Tuge, the Huangzhong volunteers, and the eight Qiang tribes,

sentences.zh: 〈義從、八種並見

translations.literal: 〈Volunteer followers and eight kinds both appear in
translations.idiomatic: 〈See the treatises on volunteer followers and the eight tribes in

sentences.zh: 〈西羌傳〉。〉

translations.literal: 〈the Treatise on the Western Qiang〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈the Treatise on the Western Qiang〉

sentences.zh: 而明公擁之，以爲爪牙，譬驅虎兕以赴犬羊。

translations.literal: while my lord embraces them and makes them claws and fangs; it is like driving tigers and rhinos to pursue dogs and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: You hold them as your claws and fangs—it would be like setting tigers on sheep.

sentences.zh: 七也。

translations.literal: This is seven.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh point.

sentences.zh: 又明公將帥皆中表腹心，周旋日乆，恩信淳著，忠誠可任，智謀可恃。

translations.literal: Moreover my lord's generals and commanders are all inner and outer heart and belly, have moved in circles for a long day; grace and trust are thickly evident; loyalty and devotion may be entrusted; wisdom and stratagem may be relied on.
translations.idiomatic: Your commanders are kinsmen and trusted followers long tested together; their loyalty and counsel are beyond question—

sentences.zh: 以膠固之衆，

translations.literal: with a host glued solid,
translations.idiomatic: with an army bound fast by mutual trust—

sentences.zh: 〈膠亦固也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Glued also means solid.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Comment: the word rendered glued here means firmly joined.〉

sentences.zh: 當解合之埶，猶以烈風掃彼枯葉。

translations.literal: to meet a situation of coming apart in combination, is still like using a fierce wind to sweep their withered leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Pitted against a loose alliance, your host would be like a gale stripping dead leaves. That is the eighth point.

sentences.zh: 八也。

translations.literal: This is eight.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth point.

sentences.zh: 夫戰有三亡，以亂攻理者亡，以邪攻正者亡，以逆攻順者亡。

translations.literal: In war there are three ways to perish: with disorder to attack order perishes; with deviance to attack the straight perishes; with rebellion to attack compliance perishes.
translations.idiomatic: There are three doomed ways to fight: disorder against order, wickedness against right, rebellion against legitimacy—

sentences.zh: 今明公秉國平正，討滅宦豎，忠義克立。

translations.literal: Now my lord holds the state even and upright, punishes and destroys the palace slaves; loyal righteousness is able to be established.
translations.idiomatic: you hold the government straight, you have destroyed the eunuchs, and you stand on loyalty and justice—

sentences.zh: 以此三德，待彼三亡，奉辭伐罪，誰敢禦之！

translations.literal: with these three virtues to await their three perishings, bearing the mandate to punish crimes—who dares withstand you!
translations.idiomatic: three virtues against their three faults; who could withstand a punitive expedition bearing the right words?

sentences.zh: 九也。

translations.literal: This is nine.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth point.

sentences.zh: 東州鄭玄學該古今，

translations.literal: In the eastern province Zheng Xuan's learning comprehends ancient and modern;
translations.idiomatic: In the east Zheng Xuan's learning spans antiquity and the present—

sentences.zh: 〈玄，北海人，故云東州。〉

translations.literal: Xuan was a man of Beihai, therefore it says eastern province.〉
translations.idiomatic: Note: he was from Beihai, hence "eastern province".〉

sentences.zh: 北海邴原清高直亮，

translations.literal: Bing Yuan of Beihai is lofty, pure, straight, and bright;
translations.idiomatic: Bing Yuan of Beihai is noted for integrity and candor—

sentences.zh: 〈《魏志》，原字根矩，北海朱虛人也。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Records: Yuan's courtesy name Genju; he was a man of Zhuxu in Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei Records gives his style as Genju and his home as Zhuxu in Beihai—

sentences.zh: 與管寧俱以操尚稱。〉

translations.literal: Together with Guan Ning he was famed for conduct and aspiration.〉
translations.idiomatic: and says he was ranked with Guan Ning for high character.〉

sentences.zh: 皆儒生所仰，羣士楷式。

translations.literal: Both are what Confucian scholars look up to, models for the host of gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Both are beacons for scholars and models for the gentry—

sentences.zh: 彼諸將若詢其計畫，足知彊弱。

translations.literal: if those generals consult their plans, it is enough to know strong and weak.
translations.idiomatic: if your opponents consulted such men, they would know their own weakness.

sentences.zh: 且燕、趙、齊、梁非不盛也，終滅於秦；

translations.literal: Moreover Yan, Zhao, Qi, and Liang were not not flourishing, yet in the end they perished to Qin;
translations.idiomatic: Yan, Zhao, Qi, and Liang were mighty states, yet Qin swallowed them all—

sentences.zh: 吳、楚七國非不衆也，卒敗滎陽。

translations.literal: The Wu and Chu seven states were not not numerous; in the end they were defeated at Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu-Chu coalition raised vast armies yet was crushed at Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 〈《前書》吳王濞、楚王戊、趙王遂、淄川王賢、濟南王辟光、膠西王卬、膠東王雄渠，景帝三年反，大將軍條侯周亞夫將兵破之滎陽。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Former Documents: King Pi of Wu, King Wu of Chu, King Sui of Zhao, King Xian of Zichuan, King Piguang of Jinan, King Ang of Jiaoxi, King Xiongj of Jiaodong rebelled in the third year of Emperor Jing; Grand General Marquis Tiao Zhou Yafu led troops and defeated them at Xingyang.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Former Han History names the seven rebel kings and records how Grand Commandant Zhou Yafu broke them at Xingyang in 154 BCE.〉

sentences.zh: 況今德政赫赫，股肱惟良，彼豈讚成其謀，造亂長寇哉？

translations.literal: How much more now virtuous government shines brilliantly, arms and legs are only good—how could they assist in that plot, make chaos, and lengthen bandits?
translations.idiomatic: Your virtue shines today and your ministers are able; would those eastern leaders really abet rebellion and breed banditry?

sentences.zh: 其不然。

translations.literal: It is not so.
translations.idiomatic: They would not.

sentences.zh: 十也。

translations.literal: This is ten.
translations.idiomatic: That is the tenth point.

sentences.zh: 若其所陳少有可採，無事徵兵以驚天下，使患役之民相聚爲非，弃德恃衆，自虧威重。

translations.literal: If what he set forth has even a little that may be adopted, there is no need to raise troops and alarm the realm, cause people weary of corvée to gather and do wrong, abandon virtue and rely on numbers, thereby injuring one's own awe-inspiring weight.
translations.idiomatic: If any part of my argument holds, you need not mobilize the empire, drive corvée-weary peasants into revolt, or forfeit moral authority by trusting numbers alone.

sentences.zh: 卓乃恱，以公業爲將軍，使統諸軍討擊關東。

translations.literal: Zhuo then was pleased; he made Gongye general and ordered him to command the various armies to strike the east of the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo was mollified; he named Zheng Tai a general and put him in command of the campaign against the eastern coalition.

sentences.zh: 或說卓曰：「鄭公業智略過人，而結謀外寇，今資之士馬，就其黨與，竊爲明公懼之。」

translations.literal: Someone persuaded Zhuo, saying: Lord Zheng Ye's plans surpass other men, yet he plots with outside bandits; now if you supply him soldiers and horses, to join his faction—privately for my lord I fear this."
translations.idiomatic: Someone persuaded Zhuo, saying: Lord Zheng Ye's plans surpass other men, yet he plots with outside bandits; now if you supply him soldiers and horses, to join his faction—privately for my lord I fear this."

sentences.zh: 卓乃收還其兵，留拜議郎。

translations.literal: Zhuo then recalled and took back his troops, kept him and appointed gentleman consultant.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo stripped him of command but kept him at court as a gentleman consultant.

sentences.zh: 卓旣遷都長安，天下飢亂，士大夫多不得其命。

translations.literal: After Zhuo had moved the capital to Chang'an, the realm was hungry and chaotic; great officers and literati mostly did not obtain their fate.
translations.idiomatic: After the removal to Chang'an, famine and anarchy spread and many scholar-officials perished.

sentences.zh: 而公業家有餘資，日引賔客高會倡樂，所贍救者甚衆。

translations.literal: Yet Gongye's household had surplus wealth; daily he drew guests to lofty meetings with musicians; those he aided and rescued were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tai still had means; he feasted guests nightly with music and rescued a great many people.

sentences.zh: 乃與何顒、荀攸共謀殺卓。

translations.literal: Then together with He Yong and Xun You he plotted to kill Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: He joined He Yong and Xun You in a plot to assassinate Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 事洩，顒等被執，公業脫身自武關走，東歸袁術。

translations.literal: The affair leaked; Yong and others were seized; Gongye slipped his body away, fled by Wu Pass, east returned to Yuan Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot failed, He Yong was arrested; Zheng Tai escaped through Wu Pass and fled east to Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 術上以爲楊州刺史。

translations.literal: Shu above appointed him governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu named him inspector of Yang province.

sentences.zh: 未至官，道卒，時秊四十一。

translations.literal: Before he reached office, died on the road; at the time his years were forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died en route before taking up the post, aged forty-one.

sentences.zh: 孔融字文舉，魯國人，孔子二十世孫也。

translations.literal: Kong Rong, courtesy name Wenju, was a man of Lu, the twentieth-generation descendant of Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong, styled Wenju, came from the state of Lu and was the twentieth-generation descendant of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 七世祖霸，爲元帝師，位至侍中。

translations.literal: His seventh-generation ancestor Ba was teacher to Emperor Yuan, rose to palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations back, Kong Ba had been tutor to Emperor Yuan of Former Han and rose to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 〈《前書》霸字次孺，元帝師。

translations.literal: 〈The Former Documents: Ba courtesy name Ciru, teacher to Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Former Han History identifies Kong Ba, styled Ciru, as Emperor Yuan's tutor.

sentences.zh: 解見

translations.literal: Explanation see
translations.idiomatic: See

sentences.zh: 〈孔昱傳〉。〉

translations.literal: 〈Kong Yu biography〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈the biography of Kong Yu〉

sentences.zh: 父宙，太山都尉。

translations.literal: His father Zhou was colonel of Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kong Zhou had been a colonel in Taishan commandery.

sentences.zh: 融幼有異才。

translations.literal: Rong in youth had unusual talent.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Kong Rong showed remarkable gifts.

sentences.zh: 〈融家傳曰：「兄弟七人，融第六，幼有自然之性。

translations.literal: 〈The Kong Rong family tradition says: Seven brothers; Rong was sixth; in youth he had natural character.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Kong Rong family tradition says: "Seven brothers; Rong was sixth; in youth he had natural character.

sentences.zh: 年四歲時，每與諸兄共食梨，融輒引小者。

translations.literal: At age four, whenever he ate pears together with elder brothers, Rong always took the small one.
translations.idiomatic: At four, when sharing pears with his brothers, he always chose the smallest.

sentences.zh: 大人問其故，荅曰：『我小兒，法當取小者。』

translations.literal: The elder asked the reason; he answered: I am the small child; by rule I ought to take the small one.
translations.idiomatic: When asked why, he said he was the youngest and by custom should take the smallest.

sentences.zh: 由是宗族竒之。」〉

translations.literal: Thereby the kinship group marveled at him.〉
translations.idiomatic: The whole clan marveled at the child."〉

sentences.zh: 年十歲，隨父詣京師。

translations.literal: At age ten, he followed his father to visit the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he accompanied his father to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時河南尹李膺

translations.literal: At the time the governor of Henan was Li Ying
translations.idiomatic: The governor of Henan at the time was Li Ying

sentences.zh: 〈膺，潁川襄城人。

translations.literal: 〈Ying was a man of Xiangcheng in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Comment: Li Ying came from Xiangcheng in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 融家傳曰：「聞漢中李公清節直亮，意慕之，遂造公門。」

translations.literal: The Kong family tradition says: He heard that Lord Li of Hanzhong was pure in integrity and upright, admired him in intent, then went to the lord's gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Kong family tradition says: "He heard that Lord Li of Hanzhong was pure in integrity and upright, admired him in intent, then went to the lord's gate."

sentences.zh: 李固，漢中人，爲太尉，與此傳不同也。〉

translations.literal: Li Gu was a man of Hanzhong, was grand tutor; this differs from this biography.〉
translations.idiomatic: The comment notes Li Gu of Hanzhong served as grand tutor, which disagrees with the main text here.〉

sentences.zh: 以簡重自居，不妄接士賔客，勑外自非當世名人及與通家，皆不得白。

translations.literal: He held himself grave and reserved, did not rashly receive gentlemen and guests; ordered outside that unless they were famous men of the age or tied families, none might be announced.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ying cultivated aloof dignity and admitted callers only if they were celebrated or had hereditary ties to his house.

sentences.zh: 融欲觀其人，故造膺門。

translations.literal: Rong wished to see this man; therefore went to Ying's gate.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong wished to meet him and presented himself at Li Ying's door.

sentences.zh: 語門者曰：「我是李君通家子弟。」

translations.literal: He told the gatekeeper: I am a younger of Lord Li's tied family."
translations.idiomatic: He told the gatekeeper: I am a younger of Lord Li's tied family."

sentences.zh: 門者言之。

translations.literal: The gatekeeper reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The porter carried the message inward.

sentences.zh: 膺請融，問曰：「高明祖父甞與僕有恩舊乎？」

translations.literal: Ying invited Rong and asked: Did your eminent grandfather once have old kindness with your servant?"
translations.idiomatic: Ying invited Rong and asked: Did your eminent grandfather once have old kindness with your servant?"

sentences.zh: 融曰：「然。

translations.literal: Rong said: Yes.
translations.idiomatic: Rong said: "Yes.

sentences.zh: 先君孔子與君先人李老君同德比義，而相師友，

translations.literal: My former lord Confucius and your former lord Elder Li shared virtue and compared righteousness, and were mutually teacher and friend,
translations.idiomatic: Confucius and Laozi, he said, had stood in a relation of mutual respect as teachers in the Way,

sentences.zh: 〈家語曰：「孔子謂南宮敬叔曰：『吾聞老聃博古而達今，通禮樂之源，明道德之歸，即吾之師也。

translations.literal: 〈The Family Sayings says: Confucius said to Nangong Jingshu: I have heard Laozi is broad in antiquity and penetrating in the present, comprehends the source of ritual and music, understands the return of the Way and virtue—he shall be my teacher.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Family Sayings quotes Confucius telling Nangong Jingshu that Laozi mastered antiquity, ritual, music, and the Way so fully that he would seek him as a teacher.

sentences.zh: 今將往矣。』

translations.literal: Now I am about to go.
translations.idiomatic: He was leaving to consult him.

sentences.zh: 遂至周，問禮於老聃焉。」〉

translations.literal: Then he arrived at Zhou and questioned Laozi on ritual.〉
translations.idiomatic: He traveled to Zhou and questioned Laozi on ritual.〉

sentences.zh: 則融與君累世通家。」

translations.literal: Then Rong and my lord are tied families for accumulated generations."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, he concluded, their houses had been allied for generations."

sentences.zh: 衆坐莫不歎息。

translations.literal: All seated none did not sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Every guest in the room drew a long breath in admiration.

sentences.zh: 太中大夫陳煒後至，

translations.literal: Grand counselor Chen Wei arrived afterward,
translations.idiomatic: The grand counselor Chen Wei arrived late.

sentences.zh: 〈煒音于匭反。〉

translations.literal: 〈Wei is read with the yu gui fan spelling.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Comment: the name Wei is glossed with a fanqie spelling.〉

sentences.zh: 坐中以告煒。

translations.literal: Those seated in the midst told Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Those present related the exchange to him.

sentences.zh: 煒曰：「夫人小而聦了，大未必竒。」

translations.literal: Wei said: When a person is small, clever and clear; great, not necessarily unusual."
translations.idiomatic: Wei said: When a person is small, clever and clear; great, not necessarily unusual."

sentences.zh: 融應聲曰：「觀君所言，將不早惠乎？」

translations.literal: Rong answered on the sound: Looking at your words, were you not precocious in youth?"
translations.idiomatic: Rong answered on the sound: Looking at your words, were you not precocious in youth?"

sentences.zh: 膺大笑曰：「高明必爲偉器。」

translations.literal: Ying greatly laughed and said: The eminent will surely become a great vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Ying greatly laughed and said: "The eminent will surely become a great vessel."

sentences.zh: 年十三，喪父，哀悴過毀，扶而後起，州里歸其孝。

translations.literal: At thirteen, father died; grief was excessive ruin, supported then could rise; his district returned his filiality.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he lost his father; he mourned so bitterly he had to be helped to his feet, and the neighborhood praised his filial piety.

sentences.zh: 性好學，博涉多該覽。

translations.literal: By nature he loved learning; broadly fathomed, much comprehended in reading.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and read widely with true comprehension.

sentences.zh: 山陽張儉爲中常侍侯覽所怨，覽爲刊章下州郡，

translations.literal: Zhang Jian of Shanyang was resented by regular attendant Hou Lan; Lan had an edited warrant sent down to provinces and commanderies,
translations.idiomatic: Hou Lan, a powerful eunuch, hounded Zhang Jian of Shanyang with a warrant that stripped the informer's name before it reached the commanderies.

sentences.zh: 〈刊，削也。

translations.literal: 〈Kan means cut away.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Comment: to print here means to cut away.

sentences.zh: 謂削去告人姓名。〉

translations.literal: It means cutting away the accuser's name.〉
translations.idiomatic: That is, the accuser's name was excised from the document.〉

sentences.zh: 以名捕儉。

translations.literal: By name to arrest Jian.
translations.idiomatic: The order commanded Zhang Jian seized by name.

sentences.zh: 儉與融兄襃有舊，亡抵於襃，不遇。

translations.literal: Jian had old ties with Rong's elder brother Bao; fleeing he arrived at Bao, did not meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian, an old friend of Kong Rong's elder brother Kong Bao, fled to his door but missed him.

sentences.zh: 〈抵，歸也。

translations.literal: 〈Di means return.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Comment: arrive here means to seek refuge.

sentences.zh: 融家傳「襃字文禮」也。〉

translations.literal: The Kong family tradition: Bao courtesy name Wenli.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Kong family tradition: "Bao courtesy name Wenli.〉"

sentences.zh: 時融年十六，儉少之而不告。

translations.literal: At the time Rong was sixteen; Jian thought him young and did not tell.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong was sixteen; Zhang Jian, dismissing him as a boy, kept silent about his errand.

sentences.zh: 融見其有窘色，

translations.literal: Rong saw he had a harried expression,
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong read the fugitive's distress in his face.

sentences.zh: 〈窘，迫也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Jiong means pressed.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Comment: harried means hard-pressed.〉

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「兄雖在外，吾獨不能爲君主邪？」

translations.literal: Said to him: Though my elder brother is outside, can I alone not be host for my lord?"
translations.idiomatic: Said to him: Though my elder brother is outside, can I alone not be host for my lord?"

sentences.zh: 因留舍之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he kept him in lodging.
translations.idiomatic: He took Zhang Jian in.

sentences.zh: 〈舍，止也。〉

translations.literal: 〈She means stop.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Comment: lodge means to shelter.〉

sentences.zh: 後事泄，國相以下，密就掩捕，儉得脫走，遂并收襃、融送獄。

translations.literal: Later the affair leaked; from the kingdom minister downward they secretly came to seize; Jian obtained escape and fled; then together seized Bao and Rong and sent them to prison.
translations.idiomatic: When the secret leaked, officials moved to arrest; Zhang Jian escaped, but Kong Bao and Kong Rong were thrown into jail.

sentences.zh: 二人未知所坐。

translations.literal: The two did not know what crime they sat for.
translations.idiomatic: Neither brother knew which charge applied.

sentences.zh: 融曰：「保納舍藏者，融也，當坐之。」

translations.literal: Rong said: I who protected, received, lodged, and hid him am Rong; I ought to sit for it."
translations.idiomatic: Rong said: I who protected, received, lodged, and hid him am Rong; I ought to sit for it."

sentences.zh: 襃曰：「彼來求我，非弟之過，請甘其罪。」

translations.literal: Bao said: He came seeking me; it is not my younger brother's fault; I request willingly to bear the crime."
translations.idiomatic: Bao said: He came seeking me; it is not my younger brother's fault; I request willingly to bear the crime."

sentences.zh: 吏問其母，母曰：「家事任長，妾當其辜。」

translations.literal: The clerk asked their mother; she said: Household affairs are the eldest's charge; your handmaid bears the guilt."
translations.idiomatic: The clerk asked their mother; she said: Household affairs are the eldest's charge; your handmaid bears the guilt."

sentences.zh: 一門爭死，郡縣疑不能決，乃上讞之。

translations.literal: The whole gate competed to die; commandery and county doubted and could not decide; then sent up for review.
translations.idiomatic: The whole household vied to die in one another's place, and the local court referred the case upward for review.

sentences.zh: 〈《前書音義》曰：「讞，請也，音宜傑反。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Former Documents pronunciation says: Yan means petition; read yi jie fan.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Former Documents pronunciation says: "Yan means petition; read yi jie fan.〉"

sentences.zh: 詔書竟坐襃焉。

translations.literal: The edict in the end sat for Bao.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial rescript convicted Kong Bao alone.

sentences.zh: 融由是顯名，與平原陶丘洪、陳留邊讓齊聲稱。

translations.literal: Rong by this had illustrious name; with Taoqiu Hong of Pingyuan and Bian Rang of Chenliu he shared equal fame in reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong's fame spread; he was ranked with Taoqiu Hong of Pingyuan and Bian Rang of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 州郡禮命，皆不就。

translations.literal: Commandery and prefectural ritual summons, all he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He turned down every nomination from the regions.

sentences.zh: 辟司徒楊賜府。

translations.literal: Summoned to Minister over the Masses Yang Ci's office.
translations.idiomatic: He was recruited into the bureau of Minister over the Masses Yang Ci.

sentences.zh: 時隱覈官僚之貪濁者，將加貶黜，融多舉中官親族。

translations.literal: At the time they secretly examined grasping and corrupt officials, about to add degradation and dismissal; Rong mostly nominated inner officials' kin.
translations.idiomatic: An inquiry targeted venal officials for demotion; Kong Rong submitted names that were mostly eunuchs' relatives.

sentences.zh: 尚書畏迫內寵，召掾屬詰責之。

translations.literal: The secretariat feared pressure from inner favorites; summoned clerks and subordinates and rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: The secretariat, fearing eunuch pressure, summoned the staff to rebuke them.

sentences.zh: 融陳對罪惡，言無阿撓。

translations.literal: Rong set forth and answered the crimes; his words had no bending.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong laid out the offenses without flinching.

sentences.zh: 〈撓，曲也，音乃孝反。〉

translations.literal: 〈Nao means bent; read nai xiao fan.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Comment: bending means twisting; a fanqie note follows.〉

sentences.zh: 河南尹何進當遷爲大將軍，楊賜遣融奉謁賀進，不時通，融即奪謁還府，投劾而去。

translations.literal: Governor of Henan He Jin was about to be promoted grand general; Yang Ci sent Rong to present a visit congratulating Jin; not timely passed through; Rong then seized the visiting slip, returned to office, cast impeachment and left.
translations.idiomatic: When He Jin was slated for grand general, Yang Ci sent Kong Rong with congratulations; left waiting, Kong flung down his card and resigned in protest.

sentences.zh: 河南官屬恥之，私遣劔客欲追殺融。

translations.literal: Henan subordinates were shamed by it; privately sent swordsmen wishing to pursue and kill Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin's staff were humiliated and hired assassins to kill him.

sentences.zh: 客有言於進曰：「孔文舉有重名，

translations.literal: A guest spoke to Jin saying: Kong Wenju has heavy reputation,
translations.idiomatic: A guest spoke to Jin saying: "Kong Wenju has heavy reputation,

sentences.zh: 〈融家傳曰：「客言於進曰：『孔文舉於時英雄特傑，譬諸物類，猶衆星之有北辰，百穀之有黍稷，天下莫不屬目也。』」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Kong family tradition says: The guest spoke to Jin saying: Kong Wenju among the age's heroes is especially outstanding; compared to things, he is like the North Star among the many stars, like millet and panicled millet among the hundred grains; none under heaven does not fix their eyes.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈A family tradition quotes the guest comparing Kong Rong to the polestar among stars—too celebrated to alienate.〉

sentences.zh: 將軍若造怨此人，則四方之士引領而去矣。

translations.literal: If the general makes resentment with this man, then gentlemen of the four quarters will crane necks and depart.
translations.idiomatic: To make an enemy of him would drive talented men from your banner.

sentences.zh: 不如因而禮之，可以示廣於天下。」

translations.literal: Better thereby to treat him with courtesy; can show breadth to the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Honoring him instead would broadcast your magnanimity."

sentences.zh: 進然之，旣拜而辟融，舉高第，爲侍御史。

translations.literal: Jin approved it; after promotion he summoned Rong, raised high grade, made attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin agreed, and after his promotion summoned Kong Rong, graded him top of the class, and named him attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 與中丞趙舍不同，託病歸家。

translations.literal: Not at peace with vice censor Zhao She, pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He could not work with Vice Censor Zhao She; he pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 後辟司空掾，拜中軍候。

translations.literal: Later summoned as clerk to the minister of works; appointed central army warden.
translations.idiomatic: He was later clerk in the minister of works' office and then central army warden.

sentences.zh: 在職三日，遷虎賁中郎將。

translations.literal: Three days in office, promoted tiger guard leader.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later he rose to leader of the tiger guard.

sentences.zh: 會董卓廢立，融每因對荅，輒有匡正之言。

translations.literal: When Zhuo deposed and enthroned, Rong whenever he answered in audience always had words of correction.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Kong Rong spoke in Dong Zhuo's presence after the deposition of the emperor, he offered blunt correction.

sentences.zh: 以忤卓旨，轉爲議郎。

translations.literal: For having offended Zhuo's intent, was transferred to gentleman consultant.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo sidelined him as a gentleman consultant.

sentences.zh: 時黃巾寇數州，而北海最爲賊衝，卓乃諷三府同舉融爲北海相。

translations.literal: At the time Yellow Turbans raided several provinces, but Beihai was most the bandits' thoroughfare; Zhuo then indirectly prompted the three offices jointly to nominate Rong as minister of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: As the Turbans ravaged the coast, Dong Zhuo maneuvered the three high offices into naming Kong Rong governor of Beihai—the most exposed commandery.

sentences.zh: 融到郡，收合士民，起兵講武，馳檄飛翰，引謀州郡。

translations.literal: Rong reached the commandery, gathered scholars and people, raised troops and drilled weapons, flew dispatches and flying brush, drew in planning with commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied the people, drilled troops, exchanged letters with neighboring governors, and planned a defense.

sentences.zh: 賊張饒等羣輩二十萬衆從兾州還，融逆擊，爲饒所敗，乃收散兵保朱虛縣。

translations.literal: Bandits Zhang Rao and others in a body of two hundred thousand masses returned from Ji Province; Rong struck them opposingly, was defeated by Rao, then gathered scattered troops and defended Zhuxu county.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rao led two hundred thousand men back from Ji; Kong Rong attacked them but lost, then regrouped and held Zhuxu.

sentences.zh: 稍復鳩集吏民爲黃巾所誤者男女四萬餘人，更置城邑，立學校，表顯儒術，薦舉賢良鄭玄、彭璆、邴原等。

translations.literal: Gradually again gathered officials and people misled by Yellow Turbans, men and women more than forty thousand, reset city and towns, established schools, displayed Confucian learning, recommended worthies Zheng Xuan, Peng Qiu, Bing Yuan and others.
translations.idiomatic: He slowly gathered forty thousand souls misled by the rebels, rebuilt towns, opened schools, promoted Confucian scholarship, and recommended men such as Zheng Xuan, Peng Qiu, and Bing Yuan.

sentences.zh: 〈璆音巨秋反，又音求。〉

translations.literal: 〈Qiu read ju qiu fan, also qiu.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Comment: the name Qiu is glossed with alternate fanqie readings.〉

sentences.zh: 郡人甄子然、臨孝存知名早卒，融恨不及之，乃命配食縣社。

translations.literal: Commandery men Zhen Ziran and Lin Xiucun were famous and died early; Rong hated not having reached them; then ordered them allotted victim food at the county altars of soil.
translations.idiomatic: He honored two local worthies who had died young by granting them posthumous sacrifice at the county altars.

sentences.zh: 其餘雖一介之善，莫不加禮焉。

translations.literal: As for the rest, though a single hair's worth of good, none did he not add ritual to.
translations.idiomatic: The smallest kindness never went unrewarded.

sentences.zh: 郡人無後及四方游士有死亡者，皆爲棺具而斂葬之。

translations.literal: Commandery men without posterity and roaming scholars from the four quarters who died, he all provided coffins and gathered and buried them.
translations.idiomatic: He buried childless locals and stranded scholars at his own expense.

sentences.zh: 時黃巾復來侵暴，融乃出屯都昌，

translations.literal: When the Yellow Turbans again came invading and violent, Rong then went out and encamped at Duchang,
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow Turbans raided again, Kong Rong marched out and encamped at Duchang,

sentences.zh: 〈都昌，縣，屬北海郡，故城在今青州臨朐縣東北。〉

translations.literal: 〈Duchang is a county, belonging to Beihai commandery; its old walled town is northeast of present Linqu county in Qingzhou.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Duchang county lay in Beihai commandery; its old site was northeast of present Linqu in Shandong.〉

sentences.zh: 爲賊管亥所圍。

translations.literal: He was surrounded by the bandit Guan Hai.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Guan Hai besieged him.

sentences.zh: 融逼急，乃遣東萊太史慈求救於平原相劉備。

translations.literal: Rong pressed in urgency; then he dispatched Taishi Ci of Donglai to seek aid from Minister of Pingyuan Liu Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, Kong Rong sent Taishi Ci of Donglai to beg help from Liu Bei, governor of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 〈吳志，慈字子義，東萊人也。

translations.literal: 〈The Wu Records: Ci courtesy name Ziyi; a man of Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wu chronicle identifies Taishi Ci, styled Ziyi, as a man of Donglai.

sentences.zh: 避事之遼東，北海相孔融聞而竒之，數遣人訊問其母，并致餉遺。

translations.literal: Avoiding affairs he went to Liaodong; Minister of Beihai Kong Rong heard and marveled at him, repeatedly sent men to inquire after his mother, and also sent gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He had fled trouble to Liaodong; Kong Rong, hearing of him, admired him and repeatedly sent gifts and inquiries to his mother.

sentences.zh: 時融爲管亥所圍，慈從遼東還，母謂之曰：「汝與孔北海未甞相見，至汝行後，贍恤殷勤，過於故舊。

translations.literal: At the time Rong was surrounded by Guan Hai; Ci returned from Liaodong; his mother said to him: You and Kong of the North Sea have never met; since you left, his aid and care have been diligent, more than for old friends.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Rong was surrounded by Guan Hai; Ci returned from Liaodong; his mother said to him: "You and Kong of the North Sea have never met; since you left, his aid and care have been diligent, more than for old friends.

sentences.zh: 今爲賊所圍，汝宜赴之。」

translations.literal: Now he is surrounded by bandits; you ought to go to him.
translations.idiomatic: and now that he was trapped he must go to his aid."

sentences.zh: 慈單步見融，旣而求救於劉備，得兵以解圍焉。〉

translations.literal: Ci on foot alone saw Rong; then sought aid from Liu Bei, obtained troops and thereby lifted the siege.〉
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci went alone to Kong Rong, then won troops from Liu Bei and broke the siege.〉

sentences.zh: 備驚曰：「孔北海乃復知天下有劉備邪？」

translations.literal: Bei said in alarm: Kong of the North Sea then again knows there is Liu Bei under heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Bei said in alarm: Kong of the North Sea then again knows there is Liu Bei under heaven?"

sentences.zh: 即遣兵三千救之，賊乃散走。

translations.literal: He immediately dispatched three thousand troops to save him; the bandits then scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He sent three thousand men at once; the rebels fled.

sentences.zh: 時袁、曹方盛，而融無所協附。

translations.literal: At the time Yuan and Cao were flourishing, yet Rong had nothing he joined to.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao and Cao Cao were rising to power, but Kong Rong sided with neither.

sentences.zh: 左丞祖者，稱有意謀，勸融有所結納。

translations.literal: Zuo Cheng Zu, styled as having plans and counsel, urged Rong to form some ties.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Zuo Chengzu, reputed for counsel, urged Kong Rong to build alliances.

sentences.zh: 融知紹、操終圖漢室，不欲與同，故怒而殺之。

translations.literal: Rong knew Shao and Cao in the end plotted the Han house; he did not wish to be with them; therefore in anger killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong knew Yuan Shao and Cao Cao meant to supplant the Han; refusing to join them, he slew Zuo Chengzu in anger.

sentences.zh: 融負其高氣，志在靖難，而才踈意廣，迄無成功。

translations.literal: Rong bore his lofty spirit; his aim was to pacify calamity, yet talent was sparse and intent broad; in the end he had no success.
translations.idiomatic: Proud and high-minded, he meant to save the dynasty, but his talents did not match his ambitions and he achieved little.

sentences.zh: 〈迄，竟也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Qi means in the end.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Comment: the word means in the end.〉

sentences.zh: 在郡六年，劉備表領青州刺史。

translations.literal: Six years in the commandery; Liu Bei memorialized him to act as inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After six years as governor, Liu Bei had him named acting inspector of Qing province.

sentences.zh: 建安元年，爲袁譚所攻，自春至夏，戰士所餘裁數百人，流矢雨集，戈矛內接。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jian'an, he was attacked by Yuan Tan; from spring to summer the fighters remaining were only several hundred; stray arrows gathered like rain; spears clashed within.
translations.idiomatic: In 196 CE Yuan Tan attacked him; from spring into summer only a few hundred defenders remained under a storm of arrows and close combat.

sentences.zh: 融隱几讀書，

translations.literal: Rong leaned on the armrest and read books,
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong leaned on his lectern and read,

sentences.zh: 〈隱，憑也。

translations.literal: 〈Yin means lean on.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Comment: lean here means to rest upon.

sentences.zh: 《莊子》曰：「南郭子綦隱几而坐。」〉

translations.literal: The Zhuangzi says: Nanguo Ziqi leaned on the armrest and sat.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuangzi says: "Nanguo Ziqi leaned on the armrest and sat.〉"

sentences.zh: 談笑自若。

translations.literal: Talked and laughed as if nothing were wrong.
translations.idiomatic: He talked and laughed as if at ease.

sentences.zh: 城夜陷，乃奔東山，妻子爲譚所虜。

translations.literal: The city fell by night; then he fled to the eastern hills; wife and children were captured by Tan.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell by night; he fled to the eastern hills while Yuan Tan seized his family.

sentences.zh: 及獻帝都許，徵融爲將作大匠，遷少府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xian established the capital at Xu, Rong was summoned minister of imperial construction, promoted lesser treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved to Xu, Kong Rong was recalled as minister of imperial construction and then promoted to lesser treasury.

sentences.zh: 每朝會訪對，融輒引正定議，公卿大夫皆隷名而已。

translations.literal: Whenever at court assembly he was consulted in reply, Rong always cited correctness and fixed deliberation; dukes, ministers, and great officers only appended names.
translations.idiomatic: At court conferences he set the terms of debate while high officials merely signed their names to his conclusions.

sentences.zh: 〈《說文》云：「隷，附著。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Shuowen says: Li means attach.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Shuowen says: "Li means attach.〉"

sentences.zh: 初，太傅馬日磾奉使山東，及至淮南，數有意於袁術。

translations.literal: In the beginning, Grand Tutor Ma Midi was sent on mission east of the mountains; when he reached Huainan, repeatedly he had intent toward Yuan Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Ma Midi had been sent east; reaching Huainan he showed repeated favor to Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 術輕侮之，遂奪取其節，求去又不聽，因欲逼爲軍帥。

translations.literal: Shu despised and insulted him; then seized and took his credentials; he sought to leave but was not permitted; then wished to force him to be army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu humiliated him, seized his baton of office, refused his resignation, and tried to force him to command troops.

sentences.zh: 日磾深自恨，遂嘔血而斃。

translations.literal: Midi deeply hated himself; then vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Midi died of shame and a hemorrhage.

sentences.zh: 〈三輔決錄曰：「日磾字翁叔，馬融之族子。

translations.literal: 〈The Sanfu Judgment Record says: Midi courtesy name Wengshu; a clan nephew of Ma Rong.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Sanfu Judgment Record says: "Midi courtesy name Wengshu; a clan nephew of Ma Rong.

sentences.zh: 少傳融業，以才學進。

translations.literal: In youth transmitted Rong's learning; by talent and learning advanced.
translations.idiomatic: trained under Kong Rong in youth and rose by scholarship,

sentences.zh: 與楊彪、盧植、蔡邕等典校中書，歷位九卿，遂登台輔。」

translations.literal: Together with Yang Biao, Lu Zhi, Cai Yong and others collated the palace archives; passed through the nine ministers; then ascended to terrace and aid.
translations.idiomatic: collated the archives with Yang Biao, Lu Zhi, and Cai Yong, rose through the nine ministers, and reached the highest councils,"

sentences.zh: 獻帝春秋曰：「術從日磾借節觀之，因奪不還，條軍中十餘人使促辟之。

translations.literal: The Annals of Emperor Xian says: Shu from Midi borrowed credentials to view them, then seized and did not return; listed more than ten men in the army to urge summoning him.
translations.idiomatic: The Annals of Emperor Xian says: "Shu from Midi borrowed credentials to view them, then seized and did not return; listed more than ten men in the army to urge summoning him.

sentences.zh: 日磾謂術曰：『卿先代諸公辟士云何？

translations.literal: Midi said to Shu: How did your former generation's dukes summon gentlemen?
translations.idiomatic: Ma Midi asked how the great houses of Yuan Shu's line had ever summoned men by coercion,

sentences.zh: 而言促之，謂公府掾可劫得乎？』

translations.literal: yet you speak of urging them—do you think bureau clerks can be seized by force?
translations.idiomatic: and whether high bureau clerks could be dragooned,

sentences.zh: 從術求去，而術不遣，旣以失節屈辱憂恚。」〉

translations.literal: He sought leave from Shu but Shu would not send him; then by losing his credentials he suffered humiliation and grief.〉
translations.idiomatic: then begged to leave but was held until shame and rage killed him."〉

sentences.zh: 及喪還，朝廷議欲加禮。

translations.literal: When the mourning returned, the court deliberated wishing to add rites.
translations.idiomatic: When his body came home, the court debated granting him special funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 融乃獨議曰：「日磾以上公之尊，秉髦節之使，銜命直指，

translations.literal: Rong alone deliberated, saying: Midi by the honor of upper duke, bearing credentials of yak-tail envoy, bearing mandate straight-pointing,
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong alone objected: "as a grandee bearing the imperial baton on a direct commission,

sentences.zh: 〈直指，無屈撓也。

translations.literal: 〈Straight-pointing means without bending.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Comment: direct commission means without deviation,

sentences.zh: 《前書》有繡衣直指。〉

translations.literal: The Former Documents has embroidered-clothes straight-pointing.〉
translations.idiomatic: as in the Former Han embroidered-guard commissioners,〉

sentences.zh: 寧輯東夏，

translations.literal: to pacify and gather the eastern summer,
translations.idiomatic: he should have pacified the east,

sentences.zh: 〈輯，和也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Ji means harmonize.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Comment: gather here means to harmonize,〉

sentences.zh: 而曲媚姦臣，爲所牽率，章表署用，輒使首名，

translations.literal: yet bent to flatter a treacherous minister, was led along by him; memorials and appointments always made his name first,
translations.idiomatic: yet he curried favor with a traitor, let himself be led, and lent his name first on every memorial and appointment,

sentences.zh: 〈所上章表及署補用，皆以日磾名爲首也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Memorials submitted and appointments signed all took Midi's name as head.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈meaning Ma Midi's signature headed every document,〉

sentences.zh: 附下罔上，

translations.literal: cleaving to those below and deceiving those above,
translations.idiomatic: cleaving to inferiors while deceiving the throne—

sentences.zh: 〈前書曰：「附下罔上者刑。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Former Documents says: Those who cleave below and deceive above are punished.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Former Han law punished those who flattered subordinates while deceiving superiors,〉

sentences.zh: 姦以事君。

translations.literal: treacherously serving the lord.
translations.idiomatic: and treason in serving the ruler,

sentences.zh: 〈《左傳》叔向曰：「姦以事君者，吾所能禦。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Zuo Tradition: Shu Xiang said: Those who treacherously serve the lord—such I can withstand.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈as Shu Xiang says in the Zuo Tradition,〉

sentences.zh: 昔國佐當晉軍而不撓，

translations.literal: In old days Guo Zhuo faced the Jin army without bending,
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhuo once faced the Jin host unbowed,

sentences.zh: 〈《公羊傳》曰：「鞌之戰，齊師大敗。

translations.literal: 〈The Gongyang Tradition says: At the battle of An the Qi army was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: 〈the Gongyang chronicle on the battle of An:

sentences.zh: 齊侯使國佐如師。

translations.literal: The marquis of Qi sent Guo Zhuo to the army.
translations.idiomatic: the marquis of Qi sent Guo Zhuo to the enemy camp,

sentences.zh: 郤克曰：『與我紀侯之甗及魯、衞之侵地，使耕者東西其畝，以蕭同叔子爲質，則吾舍子。』

translations.literal: Xi Ke said: Give me the tripod of Marquis Ji and Lu and Wei's invaded lands, make plowmen east-west their furrows, take Lady Xiao Tongshu as hostage—then I release you.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Ke demanded the tripod of Ji, border lands from Lu and Wei, reoriented fields, and the marquis's mother as hostage,

sentences.zh: 國佐曰：『與我紀侯之甗，請諾。

translations.literal: Guo Zhuo said: Give me the tripod of Marquis Ji—I request assent.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhuo conceded the tripod,

sentences.zh: 使反魯、衞之侵，請諾。

translations.literal: Make return Lu and Wei's invasions—I request assent.
translations.idiomatic: promised to return Lu's and Wei's lands,

sentences.zh: 使耕者東西其畝，是則土齊也。

translations.literal: Make plowmen east-west their furrows—that is to treat Qi as soil.
translations.idiomatic: but called east-west furrows an attempt to reduce Qi to a subject soil,

sentences.zh: 蕭同叔子者，齊君母也，齊君母猶晉君之母也，曰不可。

translations.literal: Lady Xiao Tongshu is the Qi lord's mother; the Qi lord's mother is like the Jin lord's mother—said not possible.
translations.idiomatic: and refused to hand over the marquis's mother, likening her to the Jin ruler's own mother,

sentences.zh: 請戰，一戰而不勝，請再戰，再戰而不勝，請三戰，三戰不勝，則齊國盡子之有也，何必蕭同叔子爲質！』

translations.literal: I request battle: one battle if not victorious, request second battle; second if not victorious, request third; if three battles not victorious, then the state of Qi is wholly yours—why must Lady Xiao Tongshu be hostage!
translations.idiomatic: then offered three battles to decide the fate of Qi rather than yield the hostage,

sentences.zh: 揖而去之。」〉

translations.literal: bowed and left.〉
translations.idiomatic: and withdrew with a bow.〉

sentences.zh: 宜僚臨白刃而正色。

translations.literal: Yuan Liao faced bare blades with correct color.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Liao kept his composure under naked blades,

sentences.zh: 〈楚白公勝欲爲亂，謂石乞曰：「王卿士皆以五百人當之則可。」

translations.literal: 〈Chu Duke Bai Sheng wished to rebel; said to Shi Qi: If king and ministers all with five hundred men oppose him then it can be done.
translations.idiomatic: 〈when Bai Gong of Chu plotted revolt and told Shi Qi that five hundred men could hold each minister,

sentences.zh: 乞曰：「不可得也。」

translations.literal: Qi said: Cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Qi said it could not be done,

sentences.zh: 曰：「市南有熊相宜僚者，若得之，可以當五百人矣。」

translations.literal: Said: South of the market is Xiong Yi Yuan Liao; if you obtain him, he can match five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: and named the warrior Yuan Liao south of the market as worth five hundred,

sentences.zh: 乃從白公而見之。

translations.literal: Then followed Bai Gong and saw him.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Gong went to see him,

sentences.zh: 與言，恱；

translations.literal: spoke with him, pleased;
translations.idiomatic: spoke with him and was pleased,

sentences.zh: 告之故，辭；

translations.literal: told him the reason, declined;
translations.idiomatic: explained the plot; Yuan Liao refused,

sentences.zh: 承之以劔，不動。

translations.literal: presented him with sword; unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: and even a sword at his breast did not move him—

sentences.zh: 事見左傳。〉

translations.literal: The affair appears in the Zuo Tradition.〉
translations.idiomatic: as the Zuo Tradition records.〉

sentences.zh: 王室大臣，豈得以見脅爲辭！

translations.literal: A great minister of the royal house—how can he take being coerced as excuse!
translations.idiomatic: A minister of the royal house cannot plead coercion as excuse.

sentences.zh: 又袁術僭逆，非一朝一夕，日磾隨從，周旋歷歲。

translations.literal: Moreover Yuan Shu's usurpation and rebellion was not one morning and evening; Midi followed and moved in circles for years.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu's treason was no overnight affair; Ma Midi had attended him for years.

sentences.zh: 漢律與罪人交關三日已上，皆應知情。

translations.literal: Han statute: associating with a guilty man three days or more—all should be deemed knowing.
translations.idiomatic: Han law held anyone who consorted with criminals three days or more complicit,

sentences.zh: 春秋魯叔孫得臣卒，以不發揚襄仲之罪，貶不書日。

translations.literal: In the Spring and Autumn, when Lu's Shusun Dechen died, for not exposing Duke Xiangzhong's crime, demotion—day not written.
translations.idiomatic: the Spring and Autumn omits the day of Shusun Dechen's death because he hid Prince Sui's crime,

sentences.zh: 〈《公羊傳》曰：「叔孫得臣卒。」

translations.literal: 〈The Gongyang Tradition says: Shusun Dechen died.
translations.idiomatic: 〈the Gongyang says Shusun Dechen died,

sentences.zh: 何休注曰：「不日者，知公子遂欲殺君，而爲人臣知賊而不言，明當誅也。」

translations.literal: He Xiu's commentary says: Not dated—knowing Prince Sui wished to kill the lord, yet as minister knowing the villain and not speaking—clearly ought to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: and He Xiu explains the omission of the day: he knew Prince Sui would murder the duke yet stayed silent,

sentences.zh: 公子遂即襄仲也。〉

translations.literal: Prince Sui is Duke Xiangzhong.〉
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sui being Duke Xiangzhong of Lu.〉

sentences.zh: 鄭人討幽公之亂，斲子家之棺。

translations.literal: The Zheng people punished Duke You's chaos, hacked Zijia's coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng hacked open Zijia's coffin over Duke You's murder,

sentences.zh: 〈《左傳》：「鄭子家卒，鄭人討幽公之亂，斲子家之棺而逐其族。」

translations.literal: 〈The Zuo Tradition: When Zheng Zijia died, the Zheng people punished Duke You's chaos, hacked Zijia's coffin and expelled his clan.
translations.idiomatic: 〈the Zuo Tradition records Zheng punishing Zijia's clan after Duke You's death,

sentences.zh: 杜預注曰：「斲薄其棺，不使從卿禮。」

translations.literal: Du Yu's commentary says: Hacked thin his coffin, did not let him follow minister ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu notes they thinned his coffin so he could not receive ministerial burial,

sentences.zh: 爲其殺君故也。〉

translations.literal: because he killed the lord.〉
translations.idiomatic: for his part in regicide.〉

sentences.zh: 聖上哀矜舊臣，未忍追案，不宜加禮。」

translations.literal: The sage above pities old ministers, has not yet borne to pursue the case; rites ought not be added."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pities old servants and will not reopen the case; he should not be honored beyond the usual."

sentences.zh: 朝廷從之。

translations.literal: The court followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted Kong Rong's view.

sentences.zh: 時論者多欲復肉刑。

translations.literal: At the time many in public debate wished to restore corporal mutilation.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many officials wanted to restore corporal mutilation.

sentences.zh: 融乃建議曰：「古者敦庬，善否不別，《左傳》楚申叔時曰：「人生敦庬。」

translations.literal: Kong Rong thereupon submitted a proposal, saying: "In high antiquity they were simple and vast; good and evil were not distinguished—the Zuo Commentary, Chu's Shen Shushi said: 'Human life is simple and vast.'
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong argued: "In antiquity life was plain and simple; good and evil were not sharply divided. Shen Shushi of Chu said in the Zuo Commentary: 'Human life is simple and vast.'

sentences.zh: 杜預注：「庬，厚大也。」

translations.literal: Du Yu annotates: 'Kuang means thick and great.'
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu glosses kuang as thick and great.

sentences.zh: 吏端刑清，端，直也。

translations.literal: Clerks were upright and punishments were clear—duan means upright.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were upright and punishments were clear—duan means upright.

sentences.zh: 政無過失。

translations.literal: Government had no errors.
translations.idiomatic: Government ran without fault.

sentences.zh: 百姓有罪，皆自取之。

translations.literal: When the common people had guilt they all brought it on themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When commoners sinned, they brought it on themselves.

sentences.zh: 末世陵遲，風化壞亂，政撓其俗，法害其人。

translations.literal: In declining ages slopes slip; customs spoil and disorder; government bends custom; law injures the people.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages decay: morale frays, institutions warp until policy twists customs and statutes harm the people.

sentences.zh: 故曰上失其道，民散乆矣。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: when those above lose the Way, the people scatter—long ago.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying that once rulers abandon the Way, their subjects drift beyond recall.

sentences.zh: 而欲繩之以古刑，投之以殘弃，殘其支體而弃廢之。

translations.literal: Yet wishing to tie them to ancient punishments and cast them away as wreckage—mutilating their limbs and casting them off as ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you would bind them to ancient mutilations, maim their limbs, and cast them aside as ruined bodies.

sentences.zh: 非所謂與時消息者也。

translations.literal: This is not what is called ebbing and flowing with the age.
translations.idiomatic: That is not what it means to breathe with the times.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「天地盈虛，與時消息。」

translations.literal: The Changes says: "Heaven and earth wax and wane, ebbing and flowing with the age."
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says: "Heaven and earth wax and wane with the seasons."

sentences.zh: 紂斮朝涉之脛，天下謂爲無道。

translations.literal: Zhou cut the shin of a man wading the ford at dawn—the realm called him devoid of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhou cut the shins of a man wading at dawn, and the realm judged him devoid of the Way.

sentences.zh: 《尚書》曰：「紂斮朝涉之脛。」

translations.literal: The Documents says: "Zhou cut the shin of a man wading at dawn."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says: "Zhou cut the shin of a man wading at dawn."

sentences.zh: 孔安國注曰：「冬日見朝涉水者，謂其脛耐寒，斮而視之。」

translations.literal: Kong Anguo annotates: "In winter he saw a man wading at dawn, judged his shins able to endure cold, cut them and looked."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Anguo glosses: "In winter he saw a man wading at dawn, thought his shins must resist cold, cut them, and looked."

sentences.zh: 夫九牧之地，千八百君，《前書》賈山曰：「昔者周蓋千八百國，以九州之人養千八百君也。」

translations.literal: Across the Nine Pastures' lands were eighteen hundred lords—the Former Documents, Jia Shan said: "Formerly Zhou had roughly eighteen hundred states; the people of the Nine Provinces nourished eighteen hundred lords."
translations.idiomatic: Across the Nine Pastures were eighteen hundred lords. Jia Shan said in the Former Documents: "Zhou once had some eighteen hundred states; the people of the Nine Provinces fed eighteen hundred rulers."

sentences.zh: 若各刖一人，是下常有千八百紂也。

translations.literal: If each severed one foot, below there would constantly be eighteen hundred Zhous.
translations.idiomatic: If each lord amputated one man, the land would forever harbor eighteen hundred tyrants like Zhou.

sentences.zh: 求俗休和，弗可得已。

translations.literal: Seeking customs at rest and harmony cannot be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Peace and harmony could never be achieved.

sentences.zh: 且被刑之人，慮不念生，志在思死，類多趨惡，莫復歸正。

translations.literal: Moreover those who have suffered punishment do not plan on living; their hearts dwell on death; most incline toward evil and never return to rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: The branded stop investing in survival; hope dies, recidivism rises, and rehabilitation falters.

sentences.zh: 夙沙亂齊，左傳曰，靈公廢太子光，立公子牙，使高厚傅牙，夙沙衞爲少傅。

translations.literal: Su Sha threw Qi into chaos—the Zuo Commentary says Duke Ling deposed Crown Prince Guang, enthroned Prince Ya, made Gao Hou tutor to Ya, and Su Sha Wei junior tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Su Sha threw Qi into chaos. The Zuo Commentary says Duke Ling deposed Crown Prince Guang, enthroned Prince Ya, made Gao Hou tutor to Ya, and Su Sha Wei junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 崔杼逆光而立之，是爲莊公。

translations.literal: Cui Shu restored Guang and enthroned him—this was Duke Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Shu restored Guang and enthroned him as Duke Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 莊公以夙沙衞易己，衞奔高唐以叛。

translations.literal: Duke Zhuang because Su Sha Wei had replaced him—Wei fled to Gaotang and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhuang resented Su Sha Wei for having replaced him; Wei fled to Gaotang and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 伊戾禍宋，《左傳》，楚客聘于晉，過宋，太子痤知之，請野享之。

translations.literal: Yi Li harmed Song—the Zuo Commentary: a guest of Chu was on mission to Jin and passed through Song; Crown Prince Zuo learned of it and asked for an outdoor feast.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Li brought disaster on Song. A Chu envoy bound for Jin passed through Song; Crown Prince Zuo learned of it and asked for an outdoor feast.

sentences.zh: 公使往，伊戾請從，遣之。

translations.literal: The duke sent him; Yi Li asked to accompany and was dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: The duke sent the prince; Yi Li asked to go along and was sent.

sentences.zh: 至則欿用牲，加書徵之，騁而告曰：「太子將爲亂，旣與楚客盟矣。」

translations.literal: On arrival he improperly used sacrificial victims, added a written summons, and galloped back to report: "The crown prince is about to rebel—he has already allied with the Chu guest."
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he improperly sacrificed, added a written summons, and galloped back to report: "The crown prince is plotting rebellion and has already allied with the Chu envoy."

sentences.zh: 公使視之，則信有焉。

translations.literal: The duke sent men to look—sure enough there was evidence.
translations.idiomatic: The duke sent men to investigate and found apparent proof.

sentences.zh: 公囚太子，太子縊死。

translations.literal: The duke imprisoned the crown prince; the crown prince hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: The duke imprisoned the crown prince, who hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 公徐聞其無罪，乃亨伊戾。

translations.literal: The duke slowly learned he was innocent and then boiled Yi Li.
translations.idiomatic: The duke slowly learned the prince was innocent and boiled Yi Li alive.

sentences.zh: 趙高、英布爲世大患。

translations.literal: Zhao Gao and Ying Bu became great scourges to the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gao and Ying Bu became great scourges of their age.

sentences.zh: 《史記》，胡亥謂李斯曰：「高，故宮人也。」

translations.literal: The Records: Hu Hai said to Li Si, "Gao is a former palace man."
translations.idiomatic: The Records says Hu Hai told Li Si: "Gao is a former palace eunuch."

sentences.zh: 遂專信任之。

translations.literal: He thereupon trusted him exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Hai then trusted him exclusively.

sentences.zh: 後殺李斯，劫殺胡亥，卒亡秦也。

translations.literal: Later he killed Li Si, coerced and killed Hu Hai, and in the end destroyed Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He later killed Li Si, forced Hu Hai's death, and in the end destroyed Qin.

sentences.zh: 《前書》，英布坐法黥，論輸驪山，亡之江中爲羣盜。

translations.literal: The Former Documents: Ying Bu by law was tattooed, sentenced and sent to Mount Li, fled to the river and became a bandit chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Documents says Ying Bu was tattooed by law, sent to Mount Li, fled to the rivers, and became a bandit chief.

sentences.zh: 及屬項羽，常爲先鋒陷陣。

translations.literal: When he came under Xiang Yu he was constantly vanguard breaking formations.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiang Yu he often led the vanguard in breaking enemy lines.

sentences.zh: 後歸漢，爲九江王。

translations.literal: Later he returned to Han and became king of Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Han and became king of Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 謀反，誅之。

translations.literal: He plotted rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He rebelled and was executed.

sentences.zh: 不能止人遂爲非也，適足絕人還爲善耳。

translations.literal: They cannot stop others from thus doing wrong—they only suffice to cut people off from returning to good.
translations.idiomatic: Corporal shame does not deter crime; it simply bars redemption.

sentences.zh: 雖忠如鬻拳，左傳：「初，鬻拳彊諫，楚子弗從。

translations.literal: Though loyal like Yu Quan—the Zuo Commentary: "At first Yu Quan strongly remonstrated; the ruler of Chu would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Men as loyal as Yu Quan—the Zuo Commentary: "At first Yu Quan strongly remonstrated; the Chu ruler would not listen.

sentences.zh: 臨之以兵，懼而從之。

translations.literal: He confronted him with troops; in fear the ruler followed.
translations.idiomatic: He confronted the ruler with troops; in fear the ruler yielded.

sentences.zh: 拳曰：『吾懼君以兵，罪莫大焉。』

translations.literal: Quan said: 'I frightened the ruler with troops—no crime is greater.'
translations.idiomatic: Quan said: "I frightened my ruler with troops—no crime is greater."

sentences.zh: 遂自刖。

translations.literal: He thereupon cut off his own foot.
translations.idiomatic: He then cut off his own foot.

sentences.zh: 楚人以爲大閽。

translations.literal: The people of Chu made him grand gatekeeper.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chu made him grand gatekeeper.

sentences.zh: 君子曰：『鬻拳可謂愛君矣。

translations.literal: The gentleman said: 'Yu Quan may be called one who loved his ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman said: "Yu Quan truly loved his ruler.

sentences.zh: 諫以自納於刑，刑猶不忘納君於善。』」

translations.literal: He remonstrated and submitted himself to punishment; even in punishment he did not forget to bring the ruler to good.""
translations.idiomatic: He remonstrated and submitted himself to punishment; even under punishment he sought to bring his ruler to good.""

sentences.zh: 信如卞和，《韓子》曰：「楚人和氏得璞玉於楚山之中，獻之武王。

translations.literal: Trustworthy like Bian He—the Han Feizi says: "He of the Bian clan in Chu obtained raw jade in the mountains of Chu and presented it to King Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Trustworthy like Bian He—the Han Feizi says: "Bian He of Chu found raw jade in the Chu mountains and presented it to King Wu.

sentences.zh: 武王使玉人相之，曰：『石也。』

translations.literal: King Wu had a jade appraiser examine it; he said: 'It is stone.'
translations.idiomatic: King Wu had a jade appraiser examine it; the man said: "It is stone."

sentences.zh: 王以和爲謾己，刖其左足。

translations.literal: The king thought He had deceived him and cut off his left foot.
translations.idiomatic: The king thought He had deceived him and cut off his left foot.

sentences.zh: 及文王即位，和又奉其璞，玉人又曰：『石也。』

translations.literal: When King Wen took the throne, He again presented his raw jade; the jade appraiser again said: 'It is stone.'
translations.idiomatic: When King Wen took the throne, He again presented the jade; the appraiser again said: "It is stone."

sentences.zh: 又刖其右足。

translations.literal: They again cut off his right foot.
translations.idiomatic: They again cut off his right foot.

sentences.zh: 文王薨，成王即位，和乃抱其璞而哭於楚山之下，三日三夜，泣盡而繼以血。

translations.literal: When King Wen died and King Cheng took the throne, He then embraced his raw jade and wept at the foot of the Chu mountains for three days and three nights; tears exhausted, blood followed.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wen died and King Cheng took the throne, He embraced the jade and wept at the Chu mountains for three days and three nights until tears gave way to blood.

sentences.zh: 王使玉人攻璞而得寶焉。」
