translations.literal: The king sent the jade appraiser to work the raw jade and obtained a treasure."
translations.idiomatic: The king had the jade worked and obtained a treasure."

sentences.zh: 琴操曰：「荊王封和爲陵陽侯，和辭不就而去。

translations.literal: The Qincao says: "The king of Jing enfeoffed He as Marquis of Lingyang; He declined and would not accept, and left.
translations.idiomatic: The Qincao says: "The king of Jing enfeoffed He as Marquis of Lingyang; He declined and left.

sentences.zh: 乃作怨歌曰：『進寶得刑，足離分兮。

translations.literal: He then composed a song of grievance: 'Presenting treasure yet receiving punishment—feet parted and divided!
translations.idiomatic: He composed a lament: "Presenting treasure yet punished—feet torn apart!

sentences.zh: 去封立信，守休芸兮。

translations.literal: Declining enfeoffment yet keeping faith—guarding rest amid fields!
translations.idiomatic: Declining rank yet keeping faith—guarding honor amid fields!

sentences.zh: 斷者不續，豈不冤兮！』」

translations.literal: What is severed cannot be joined—is this not injustice!
translations.idiomatic: What is severed cannot be joined—is this not injustice!"

sentences.zh: 智如孫臏，史記，孫臏與龐涓學兵法，涓事魏惠王爲將軍，自以能不及臏，陰使召臏，斷其兩足而黥之。

translations.literal: Wise like Sun Bin—the Records: Sun Bin and Pang Juan studied military methods together; Juan served King Hui of Wei as general, judged his ability inferior to Bin's, secretly had Bin summoned, cut off both his feet and tattooed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wise like Sun Bin—the Records: Sun Bin and Pang Juan studied military arts; Juan served Wei as general, envied Bin, had him summoned, cut off both feet, and tattooed him.

sentences.zh: 臏後入齊，威王問兵法，以爲師。

translations.literal: Later Bin entered Qi; King Wei asked about military methods and made him teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Bin later entered Qi; King Wei questioned him on strategy and made him his teacher.

sentences.zh: 魏與趙攻韓，齊使田忌將而往。

translations.literal: Wei and Zhao attacked Han; Qi sent Tian Ji to lead troops and go.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei and Zhao attacked Han, Qi sent Tian Ji to command the army.

sentences.zh: 龐涓聞，去韓而歸。

translations.literal: Pang Juan heard and left Han to return.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Juan heard and hurried back from Han.

sentences.zh: 臏謂田忌曰：「三晉之兵素悍勇而輕齊。

translations.literal: Bin told Tian Ji: "The troops of the Three Jin are by nature fierce and brave and look down on Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Bin told Tian Ji: "The Three Jin armies are fierce and despise Qi.

sentences.zh: 軍半至。

translations.literal: Half the army arrives.
translations.idiomatic: Half the army will arrive.

sentences.zh: 使齊軍入魏地爲十萬竈，明日爲五萬竈，明日爲二萬竈。」

translations.literal: Have the Qi army enter Wei territory and make one hundred thousand cooking pits; tomorrow make fifty thousand; the next day make twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Have the Qi army enter Wei and make one hundred thousand cooking pits; the next day fifty thousand; the day after twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 龐涓行三日，大喜曰：「我固知齊卒怯，入吾地三日，士卒亡者過半矣。」

translations.literal: Pang Juan marched three days and said in great joy: "I knew all along the Qi soldiers were cowards—three days in our territory and more than half the troops have fled."
translations.idiomatic: Pang Juan marched three days and exulted: "I knew Qi soldiers were cowards—three days in our land and more than half have fled."

sentences.zh: 乃棄其步兵，與其輕銳倍日并行逐之。

translations.literal: He then abandoned his infantry and with his light elite troops marched double days in parallel pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned his infantry and with light elite troops pursued at double speed.

sentences.zh: 孫子度其行，暮當至馬陵。

translations.literal: Sun Bin calculated their march—they would reach Maling at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Bin calculated their march and knew they would reach Maling at dusk.

sentences.zh: 馬陵道狹，旁多險阻，可伏兵，乃斫大樹白而書之曰「龐涓死於此木下」。

translations.literal: The Maling road was narrow with many obstacles beside it—good for ambush; he cut a large tree bare and wrote on it: "Pang Juan dies beneath this tree."
translations.idiomatic: The Maling road was narrow and treacherous—ideal for ambush. He stripped a tree and wrote: "Pang Juan dies beneath this tree."

sentences.zh: 於是令齊軍曰：「善射者萬弩，夾道而伏，期日莫見火舉而俱發。」

translations.literal: He then ordered the Qi army: "Good archers with ten thousand crossbows lie in ambush along the road; at dusk when you see fire raised, all release together."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered: "Ten thousand crossbowmen lie in ambush along the road; at dusk when fire is raised, release together."

sentences.zh: 涓夜至斫木下，見白書，乃攢火燭之，讀書未畢，齊軍萬弩俱發，魏軍大亂相失。

translations.literal: Juan by night reached the cut tree, saw the bare writing, gathered fire to illuminate it; before he finished reading, ten thousand Qi crossbows released together and the Wei army fell into great disorder and lost one another.
translations.idiomatic: Juan reached the tree at night, lit a torch to read, and before he finished ten thousand crossbows fired; the Wei army collapsed in chaos.

sentences.zh: 龐涓自知智窮兵敗，遂自剄。

translations.literal: Pang Juan knew his stratagems were exhausted and his army defeated, and cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Juan knew he was beaten and cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 曰：「遂成豎子之名矣。」

translations.literal: He said: "Thus the stripling's name is made."
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Thus the stripling wins fame."

sentences.zh: 冤如巷伯，毛萇注詩云：「巷伯，內小臣也。

translations.literal: Wronged like the Lane Uncle—Mao Chang annotates the Odes: "The Lane Uncle is an inner petty official.
translations.idiomatic: Wronged like the Lane Uncle—Mao Chang glosses the Odes: "The Lane Uncle was an inner palace official.

sentences.zh: 掌王后之命於宮中，故謂之巷伯。」

translations.literal: He transmitted the queen's commands within the palace, hence he is called the Lane Uncle.
translations.idiomatic: He carried the queen's commands within the palace, hence the name Lane Uncle."

sentences.zh: 伯被讒將刑，寺人孟子傷而作詩，以刺幽王也。

translations.literal: The Uncle was slandered and about to be punished; the eunuch Mengzi grieved and composed an ode to satirize King You.
translations.idiomatic: Slandered and facing execution, the eunuch Mengzi grieved and composed an ode satirizing King You.

sentences.zh: 才如史遷，李陵爲匈奴敗，馬遷明陵當必立功以報漢，遂被下蠶室宮刑，後乃著史記。

translations.literal: Talented like Sima Qian—Li Ling was defeated by the Xiongnu; Ma Qian knew Ling would surely establish merit to repay Han, yet was cast into the silkworm chamber and suffered palace punishment; afterward he wrote the Records.
translations.idiomatic: Talented like Sima Qian—when Li Ling was defeated by the Xiongnu, Sima Qian knew he would repay Han with merit, yet Sima Qian was cast into the silkworm chamber and mutilated; afterward he wrote the Records.

sentences.zh: 達如子政，劉向字子政。

translations.literal: Penetrating like Zizheng—Liu Xiang, courtesy name Zizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Penetrating like Liu Xiang, courtesy name Zizheng.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，上言黃金可成。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xuan he submitted that gold could be made.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan he claimed gold could be transmuted.

sentences.zh: 上令典尚方鑄作事，費甚多，方不驗，乃下吏，當死。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Director of the Imperial Workshop to cast and test; expenses were great and the method failed; he was handed to officials and deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the imperial workshop to test it; costs mounted, the method failed, and he was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 上竒其材，得踰冬減論。

translations.literal: The emperor admired his talent and was able to reduce the sentence after passing winter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his talent and reduced the sentence after winter.

sentences.zh: 班固云：「向博物洽聞，通達古今。」

translations.literal: Ban Gu said: "Xiang was broadly learned and well informed, penetrating past and present.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu said: "Xiang was broadly learned and penetrating in past and present."

sentences.zh: 一離刀鋸，沒世不齒。

translations.literal: Once they meet knife and saw, they are spurned forever.
translations.idiomatic: Once mutilated by blade and saw, they are spurned forever.

sentences.zh: 《國語》「中刑用刀鋸」也。

translations.literal: The Discourses of the States: "Intermediate punishments use knife and saw."
translations.idiomatic: The Discourses of the States says intermediate punishments use knife and saw.

sentences.zh: 是太甲之思庸，《尚書》：「太甲旣立，不明，伊尹放諸桐。

translations.literal: Therefore Taijia's reflection on the common man—the Documents: "After Taijia was enthroned he was unenlightened; Yi Yin banished him to Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Taijia who reflected on the common Way—the Documents: "Taijia was enthroned but unenlightened; Yi Yin banished him to Tong.

sentences.zh: 三年，復歸於亳。

translations.literal: After three years he returned to Bo.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he returned to Bo.

sentences.zh: 思庸。」

translations.literal: Reflection on the common man.
translations.idiomatic: He reflected on the common Way."

sentences.zh: 孔注曰：「念常道也。」

translations.literal: Kong's annotation: "Thinking on the constant Way."
translations.idiomatic: Kong's gloss: "Thinking on the constant Way."

sentences.zh: 穆公之霸秦，秦穆使孟明、白乙等伐鄭，蹇叔諫，不從。

translations.literal: Duke Mu's hegemony of Qin—Duke Mu of Qin sent Meng Ming, Bai Yi, and others to attack Zheng; Jian Shu remonstrated and was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Mu's hegemony of Qin—Duke Mu sent Meng Ming and Bai Yi against Zheng; Jian Shu remonstrated in vain.

sentences.zh: 晉襄公敗諸崤，囚孟明等，後歸之。

translations.literal: Duke Xiang of Jin defeated them at Xiao and imprisoned Meng Ming and the others; later he returned them.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xiang of Jin defeated them at Xiao, imprisoned them, and later released them.

sentences.zh: 穆公曰：「孤之罪也，夫子何罪！」

translations.literal: Duke Mu said: "My fault alone—what fault have you, sir!"
translations.idiomatic: Duke Mu said: "The fault is mine—what fault is yours!"

sentences.zh: 復使爲政，遂霸西戎。

translations.literal: He again employed them in government and thus hegemonized the Western Rong.

sentences.zh: 體謂國家之大體也。

translations.idiomatic: Ti means the great body of the state.

translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 陛級縣遠，祿位限絕，賈誼曰：「人主之尊譬如堂，羣臣如陛，衆庶如地。

sentences.zh: 故陛乃九級上，廉遠地則堂高也。」

translations.literal: It is like Heaven that cannot be climbed by steps, or sun and moon that cannot be crossed over.
translations.idiomatic: It is like Heaven that cannot be climbed or sun and moon that cannot be crossed.

sentences.zh: 《論語》曰：「夫子之不可及也，猶天之不可階而升也。」

translations.literal: The Analects says: "The Master cannot be reached—it is like Heaven that cannot be climbed by steps."
translations.idiomatic: The Analects says: "The Master cannot be reached—it is like Heaven that cannot be climbed by steps."

translations.literal: It also says: "Zhongni is like sun and moon—none can cross over him."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Confucius is like sun and moon—none can cross over him."

sentences.zh: 每有一豎臣，輒云圖之，若形之四方，形，見也。

translations.literal: Whenever there is a petty minister, they immediately say they will plot against him—as if the form were visible on four sides—xing means visible.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever some petty minister appears, men immediately say they will plot against him—as if the plot were visible on four sides—xing means visible.

sentences.zh: 非所以杜塞邪萌。

translations.literal: This is not the way to block the sprouting of evil.
translations.idiomatic: That is not how to choke off evil at its root.

translations.idiomatic: I hold that though the offense is grave, forbearance is necessary.

translations.idiomatic: What Jia Yi called "throwing at a rat yet fearing the vessel" applies here.

translations.literal: The Former Documents, Jia Yi said: "A village saying runs, 'Wishing to strike a rat yet fearing the vessel'—this is a fine analogy.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi said in the Former Documents: "A village saying runs, 'Wishing to strike a rat yet fearing the vessel'—this is a fine analogy.

translations.idiomatic: When the rat is near the vessel one still fears to strike lest the vessel be harmed—how much more when a great minister is near the ruler?"

translations.idiomatic: Duke Heng of Linhuai was Emperor Ming's brother, established in Jianwu 15, and died before advancing to princely rank.

translations.idiomatic: 〈Xuanzi being the posthumous name of Zhao Dun,

translations.idiomatic: after his death referring to Cao Pi's acceptance of the abdication,〉

translations.idiomatic: Such stern integrity ends in ruin,

translations.idiomatic: and cannot be bent in circles to cling to life,

translations.idiomatic: The Former Documents pronunciation says: "Wan means rounded smooth without corners."

translations.idiomatic: mei meaning greedy,

translations.literal: It means better to be straight and be overturned and broken, than to bend and wriggle to greedily cling to life.
translations.idiomatic: preferring ruin in integrity to survival by compromise,

translations.literal: Jia Yi said: The common sort greedily clings to life.〉
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi said: "The common sort greedily clings to life.〉"

translations.literal: Stern stern, bright bright—with kun jade and autumn frost comparing substance—such may be said.
translations.idiomatic: he may be set beside jade in a cliff and frost in autumn for purity and chill.

sentences.zh: 〈懍懍言勁烈如秋霜也。

translations.literal: <Commentary: linlin describes a stern chill like autumn frost,
translations.idiomatic: <Commentary: linlin describes a stern chill like autumn frost,

translations.idiomatic: and haohao describes firm purity like white jade,

translations.idiomatic: with a pronunciation note on hao.〉

translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu, styled Wenruo,

translations.literal: 〈Yuan Hong's Han Annals writes Yu as Yu.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Yuan Hong's Han Annals writes "Yu" as "Yu."〉

sentences.zh: 潁川潁陰人，朗陵令淑之孫也。

translations.literal: a man of Yingyin in Yingchuan, grandson of Magistrate of Langling Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He came from Yingyin in Yingchuan and was a grandson of Xun Shu, magistrate of Langling.

sentences.zh: 〈朗陵，縣，屬汝南郡，故城在今豫州朗山縣西南。〉

translations.idiomatic: 〈Langling county lay in Runan; its old site was southwest of present Langshan in Henan,〉

sentences.zh: 父緄，爲濟南相。

translations.literal: His father Gun was minister of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: his father Xun Gun having served as minister of Jinan,

sentences.zh: 〈緄音古本反。〉

translations.literal: 〈Gun read gu ben fan.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈with a pronunciation note on the name Gun,〉

sentences.zh: 緄畏憚宦官，乃爲彧娶中常侍唐衡女。

translations.literal: Gun feared and stood in awe of the eunuchs; then for Yu married the daughter of regular attendant Tang Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Gun, fearing the eunuchs, arranged a marriage for his son to the daughter of the eunuch Tang Heng,

sentences.zh: 〈《典略》曰：「衡欲以女妻汝南傅公明，公明不取，轉以妻郁。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Compendium says: Heng wished to give his daughter in marriage to Fu Gongming of Runan; Gongming would not take her; then turned to give her in marriage to Yu.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Compendium says: "Heng wished to give his daughter in marriage to Fu Gongming of Runan; Gongming would not take her; then turned to give her in marriage to Yu.〉"

sentences.zh: 彧以少有才名，故得免於譏議。

translations.literal: Yu because in youth he had a talent name, therefore obtained escape from ridicule and criticism.
translations.idiomatic: whose early reputation for talent spared him mockery for the match,

sentences.zh: 南陽何顒名知人，見彧而異之，曰：「王佐才也。」

translations.literal: He Yong of Nanyang was famed for knowing men; when he saw Yu he marveled at him, saying: A king-helper's talent.
translations.idiomatic: He Yong of Nanyang was famed for knowing men; when he saw Yu he marveled at him, saying: "A king-helper's talent."

sentences.zh: 中平六年，舉孝廉，再遷亢父令。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhongping, he was recommended filial and incorrupt, twice promoted magistrate of Kangfu.
translations.idiomatic: In 189 CE he was nominated filial and incorrupt and rose to magistrate of Kangfu,

sentences.zh: 〈亢父屬梁國，故城在今兖州任城縣南。

translations.literal: 〈Kangfu belonged to Liang state; its old walled town is south of present Rencheng county in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Kangfu lay in Liang commandery south of present Jining,

translations.idiomatic: with pronunciation notes,〉

translations.literal: At Dong Zhuo's chaos, he abandoned office and returned to his village.
translations.idiomatic: he resigned and went home when Dong Zhuo seized power,

sentences.zh: 同邵韓融時將宗親千餘家，避亂密西山中。

translations.literal: Han Rong of the same commandery at the time led more than a thousand families of kin, avoiding chaos in the western hills of Mi.
translations.idiomatic: while Han Rong of his commandery led over a thousand kinsmen into the hills west of Mi county,

sentences.zh: 〈密縣西山也。〉

translations.literal: 〈The western hills of Mi county.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈meaning the western hills of Mi,〉

sentences.zh: 彧謂父老曰：「潁川，四戰之地也。

translations.literal: Yu said to the elders: Yingchuan is a land of four battles,
translations.idiomatic: Yu said to the elders: "Yingchuan is a land of four battles,

sentences.zh: 〈四面通也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Open on four sides.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈open to attack from every direction,〉

sentences.zh: 天下有變，常爲兵衝。

translations.literal: When the realm has turmoil, it always becomes the army's thoroughfare.
translations.idiomatic: and whenever the empire rose in arms it became the main thoroughfare of armies,

sentences.zh: 密雖小固，不足以扞大難，宜亟避之。」

translations.literal: Mi though small and solid is not enough to withstand great calamity; ought urgently to flee it.
translations.idiomatic: while Mi's hills were too weak to hold off disaster and they should flee at once,"

translations.idiomatic: 〈with a pronunciation note on urgently,〉

sentences.zh: 鄉人多懷土不能去。

translations.literal: The villagers mostly clung to their soil and could not leave.
translations.idiomatic: most villagers clung to their homes and would not go,

sentences.zh: 會兾州牧同郡韓馥遣騎迎之，彧乃獨將宗族從馥，留者後多爲董卓將李傕所殺略焉。

translations.literal: It happened that Ji Province governor Han Fu of the same commandery sent riders to welcome them; Yu then alone led his clan to follow Fu; those who stayed were afterward mostly killed and plundered by Dong Zhuo's general Li Jue.
translations.idiomatic: until Han Fu of Ji province sent escort; Xun Yu alone moved his clan with Han Fu while those who stayed were later massacred or plundered by Li Jue,

translations.literal: When Yu reached Ji Province, Yuan Shao had already seized Fu's position; Shao treated Yu with the rites of a supreme guest.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Ji province Yuan Shao had displaced Han Fu and received Xun Yu as an honored guest,

sentences.zh: 彧明有意數，

translations.literal: Yu was clear in intent and reckoning,
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu saw the situation clearly and calculated the odds,

translations.literal: 〈Shu means reckoning.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈shu meaning strategic reckoning,〉

translations.literal: Seeing the Han house collapse in chaos, he always harbored the duty to aid and assist.
translations.idiomatic: and nursed a constant wish to rescue the Han,

sentences.zh: 時曹操在東郡，彧聞操有雄略，而度紹終不能定大業。

translations.literal: At the time Cao Cao was in Dong commandery; Yu heard Cao had heroic strategy, and measured that Shao in the end could not settle the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Cao Cao in Dong commandery had grand designs while Yuan Shao could never settle the realm,

sentences.zh: 初平二年，乃去紹從操。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chuping, then he left Shao and followed Cao.
translations.idiomatic: in 191 CE he left Yuan Shao for Cao Cao,

sentences.zh: 操與語大恱，曰：「吾子房也。」

translations.literal: Cao spoke with him and was greatly pleased, saying: You are my Zifang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao spoke with him and was greatly pleased, saying: "You are my Zifang."

sentences.zh: 〈比之張良。〉

translations.literal: 〈Compared to Zhang Liang.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈that is, his Zhang Liang,〉

translations.literal: He was made marshal of fierce martial; at the time his years were twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: and named him marshal of fierce martial at twenty-nine,

sentences.zh: 明年，又爲操鎮東司馬。

translations.literal: The next year, again became Cao's marshal pacifying the east.
translations.idiomatic: the next year marshal pacifying the east,

translations.literal: "Zhen" is now written "Juan," pronounced juan.
translations.idiomatic: "Zhen" is now written Juan, pronounced juan.

translations.literal: He was entrusted with affairs left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao entrusted him with affairs at home.

translations.literal: Just then Zhang Miao and Chen Gong rebelled against Cao Cao in Yan Province—the Dianlüe says: "Gong, courtesy name Gongtai, was a man of Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Zhang Miao and Chen Gong turned Yan Province against Cao Cao. The Dianlüe says: "Chen Gong, courtesy name Gongtai, came from Dong commandery.

translations.literal: Upright, stern, and bold; from youth he was linked with famous men throughout the realm."
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and bold, and from youth had ties with famous men throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 而潛迎呂布。

translations.literal: They secretly welcomed Lü Bu.
translations.idiomatic: They secretly welcomed Lü Bu.

translations.literal: Once Bu arrived, all the cities responded to him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lü Bu arrived, cities throughout the province declared for him.

sentences.zh: 邈乃使人譎彧曰：譎，詐也。

translations.literal: Miao then sent someone to deceive Xun Yu, saying—jie means to deceive:
translations.idiomatic: Miao then sent a man to trick Xun Yu—jie means to deceive:

sentences.zh: 「呂將軍來助曹使君擊陶謙，宜亟供軍實。」

translations.literal: "General Lü has come to aid Lord Cao in attacking Tao Qian—you should urgently supply military stores."
translations.idiomatic: "General Lü has come to help Lord Cao attack Tao Qian. You should urgently supply military provisions."

sentences.zh: 彧知邈有變，即勒兵設備，故邈計不行。

translations.literal: Xun Yu knew Miao had turned traitor and at once mustered troops and made preparations, so Miao's plan failed.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu knew Miao had turned traitor, mustered troops, and made preparations, so the plot failed.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史郭貢率兵數萬來到城下，求見彧。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yuzhou Guo Gong led several tens of thousands of troops to the foot of the city walls and asked to see Xun Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Yuzhou Guo Gong marched tens of thousands of men to the city and asked to meet Xun Yu.

sentences.zh: 彧將往，東郡太守夏侯惇等止之。

translations.literal: Xun Yu was about to go when Dong commandery Administrator Xiahou Dun and others stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu was about to go when Dong commandery Administrator Xiahou Dun and others stopped him.

sentences.zh: 《魏志》曰：「惇字元讓，沛國人。」

translations.literal: The Wei Records says: "Dun, courtesy name Yuanrang, was a man of Pei."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Records says: "Dun, courtesy name Yuanrang, came from Pei."

sentences.zh: 曰：「何知貢不與呂布同謀，而輕欲見之。

translations.literal: They said: "How do you know Gong is not in league with Lü Bu, yet you lightly wish to see him?
translations.idiomatic: They said: "How do you know Guo Gong is not in league with Lü Bu, yet you would go to meet him so lightly?

sentences.zh: 今君爲一州之鎮，往必危也。」

translations.literal: You are now the pillar of a whole province; if you go you will surely be in danger."
translations.idiomatic: You are the linchpin of the province—if you go, you will be in mortal danger."

sentences.zh: 彧曰：「貢與邈等分非素結，今來速者，計必未定，及其猶豫，宜時說之，縱不爲用，可使中立。

translations.literal: Xun Yu said: "Gong and Miao and the others are not old allies by nature. He has come quickly, so his plans cannot yet be settled. While he is still hesitating I should persuade him; even if he will not be used by us, we can make him remain neutral.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu replied: "Guo Gong is no longtime ally of Miao and the rest. He arrived in haste, so his plans cannot be firm yet. If I speak to him before he decides, I may not win him over—but I can at least keep him neutral.

sentences.zh: 不令其有去就也。

translations.literal: We must not let him choose sides.
translations.idiomatic: We must not let him commit to either side.

sentences.zh: 若先懷疑嫌，彼將怒而成謀，不如往也。」

translations.literal: If we show suspicion first, he will grow angry and settle on a plan—it is better to go."
translations.idiomatic: If we show suspicion first, he will take offense and commit to their side—it is better to go."

sentences.zh: 貢旣見彧無懼意，知城不可攻，遂引而去。

translations.literal: When Gong saw that Xun Yu showed no fear, he knew the city could not be taken and led his troops away.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Gong saw that Xun Yu showed no fear, he decided the city would not fall easily and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 彧乃使程昱說范、東阿，魏志：「昱字仲德，東郡東阿人。」

translations.literal: Xun Yu then sent Cheng Yu to persuade Fan and Dong'e—the Wei Records: "Yu, courtesy name Zhongde, was a man of Dong'e in Dong commandery."
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu then sent Cheng Yu to rally Fan and Dong'e. The Wei Records says: "Yu, courtesy name Zhongde, came from Dong'e in Dong commandery."

sentences.zh: 范，縣，屬東郡，今濮陽縣也。

translations.literal: Fan is a county in Dong commandery, present-day Puyang county.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was a county in Dong commandery, in present-day Puyang.

sentences.zh: 東阿，縣，屬東郡，今濟州縣也。

translations.literal: Dong'e is a county in Dong commandery, present-day Jizhou county.
translations.idiomatic: Dong'e was a county in Dong commandery, in present-day Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 使固其守，卒全三城以待操焉。

translations.literal: He made them hold firm in their defense and in the end preserved all three cities to await Cao Cao.
translations.idiomatic: He secured their defenses and in the end preserved all three cities until Cao Cao returned.

sentences.zh: 三城謂甄、范、東阿也。

translations.literal: The three cities mean Zhen, Fan, and Dong'e.
translations.idiomatic: The three cities were Juancheng, Fan, and Dong'e.

sentences.zh: 二年，陶謙死，操欲遂取徐州，還定呂布。

translations.literal: In the second year, Tao Qian died; Cao wished then to take Xu Province, then return to settle Lü Bu.
translations.idiomatic: In 194 CE, when Tao Qian died, Cao Cao meant to seize Xu province first and then deal with Lü Bu,

sentences.zh: 彧諫曰：「昔高祖保關中，

translations.literal: Yu remonstrated, saying: In old days the High Ancestor protected Guanzhong,
translations.idiomatic: Yu remonstrated, saying: "In old days the High Ancestor protected Guanzhong,

sentences.zh: 〈高祖距項羽，常留蕭何守關中。〉

translations.literal: 〈The High Ancestor resisted Xiang Yu, always left Xiao He to guard Guanzhong.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈leaving Xiao He to guard the interior while facing Xiang Yu,〉

sentences.zh: 光武據河內，皆深根固本，以制天下。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu held Henai—all deeply rooted and firm in foundation, thereby to control the realm.
translations.idiomatic: and how Guangwu held Henai to anchor his power before conquering the empire,

sentences.zh: 進可以勝敵，退足以堅守，故雖有困敗，而終濟大業。

translations.literal: Advancing can overcome enemies, withdrawing suffices to hold firm defense; therefore though there were setbacks, in the end they completed the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: both advancing to victory and retreating to a secure base, so that even reverses could not stop the great work,

sentences.zh: 將軍本以兖州首事，故能平定山東，

translations.literal: The general originally from Yanzhou began the affair, therefore was able to pacify east of the mountains,
translations.idiomatic: The general had raised his army from Yanzhou and pacified the east from that base,

sentences.zh: 〈曹操初從東郡守鮑信等迎領兖州牧，遂進兵破黃巾等，故能平定山東也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Cao Cao at first from Dong commandery guardian Bao Xin and others welcomed and took Yanzhou governor, then advanced troops and broke the Yellow Turbans, etc., therefore was able to pacify east of the mountains.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈At first Cao Cao, with the support of Dong Commandery Governor Bao Xin and others, was welcomed to take charge as Inspector of Yanzhou. He then advanced his troops and defeated the Yellow Turbans and others, and therefore was able to pacify the lands east of the mountains.〉

sentences.zh: 此實天下之要地，而將軍之關河也。

translations.literal: This is truly the realm's key ground, and the general's passes and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: making Yanzhou his strategic heartland like Guanzhong or Henai,

sentences.zh: 若不先定之，根本將何寄乎？

translations.literal: If you do not first settle it, where will root and foundation lodge?
translations.idiomatic: If it were not secured first, where would his foundation lie?

sentences.zh: 宜急分討陳宮，使虜不得西顧，乘其閒而收熟麥，約食稸穀，以資一舉，則呂布不足破也。

translations.literal: It is fitting urgently to divide and strike Chen Gong, make the foe unable to look west; seize the interval to gather ripe wheat, restrain food and stored grain, to supply one stroke—then Lü Bu is not enough to be hard to break.
translations.idiomatic: He should strike Chen Gong at once, keep Lü Bu looking east, reap the ripe wheat, hoard grain, and break Lü Bu in one blow,

sentences.zh: 今舍之而東，未見其便。

translations.literal: Now to abandon it and go east—I do not see the advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Abandoning Yanzhou for the east offered no clear gain,

sentences.zh: 多留兵則力不勝敵，少留兵則後不足固。

translations.literal: If many troops are left, strength will not overcome the enemy; if few troops are left, the rear will not suffice to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: for many troops in the east would weaken the front against Lü Bu while a small garrison could not hold Yanzhou,

sentences.zh: 布乘虛寇暴，震動人心，縱數城或全，其餘非復己有，則將軍尚安歸乎？

translations.literal: Bu will seize the void and raid violently, shake men's hearts; though several cities may be preserved, the rest will no longer be your own—then where will the general return?
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu would raid the empty province, shake morale, and even if a few towns held, the rest would be lost—where then could Cao Cao withdraw?

sentences.zh: 且前討徐州，威罰實行，其子弟念父兄之恥，必人自爲守。

translations.literal: Moreover the former campaign against Xu Province—awe and punishment were truly applied; their sons and younger brothers remember father and elder brothers' shame—they will surely each man guard for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover his last Xu campaign had been brutal; every household would fight to avenge fathers and brothers,

sentences.zh: 就能破之，尚不可保。

translations.literal: Even if able to break them, still cannot be sure of holding.
translations.idiomatic: and even victory would not guarantee holding the land,

sentences.zh: 彼若懼而相結，共爲表裏，堅壁清野，以待將軍，將軍攻之不拔，掠之無獲，不出一旬，則十萬之衆未戰而自困矣。

translations.literal: If they fear and league together, together make outer and inner, strengthen walls and clear the fields, to await the general—the general attacks yet cannot take, plunders yet obtains nothing; not beyond one ten-day week, then a hundred thousand hosts without battle will themselves be trapped.
translations.idiomatic: If the Xu men united, cleared the countryside, and held their walls, his army would find nothing to plunder and a hundred thousand men would starve within ten days without a battle,

sentences.zh: 夫事固有弃彼取此，以權一時之埶，願將軍慮焉。」

translations.literal: Affairs indeed have abandoning that and taking this, to weigh one moment's momentum—I wish the general to consider."
translations.idiomatic: The art of war sometimes means forsaking one gain for another; he begged Cao Cao to weigh it,"

sentences.zh: 操於是大收孰麥，復與布戰。

translations.literal: Cao thereupon greatly gathered ripe wheat, again fought with Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao gathered the wheat, renewed the war with Lü Bu,

sentences.zh: 布敗走，因分定諸縣，兖州遂平。

translations.literal: Bu was defeated and fled; then he divided and settled the various counties; Yanzhou was then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: defeated him, secured the counties, and pacified Yanzhou,

sentences.zh: 建安元年，獻帝自河東還洛陽，操議欲奉迎車駕，徙都於許。

translations.literal: In Jian'an 1 the emperor returned from Hedong to Luoyang; Cao Cao proposed welcoming the imperial carriage and moving the capital to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 1 (196 CE) the emperor returned from Hedong to Luoyang, and Cao Cao proposed welcoming the imperial carriage and transferring the capital to Xu.

sentences.zh: 衆多以山東未定，韓暹、楊奉負功恣睢，恣睢，肆怒貌。

translations.literal: Many held that the east of the mountains was not yet settled and that Han Xian and Yang Feng, relying on their achievements, were arrogant and overbearing—zisui means the appearance of wanton rage.
translations.idiomatic: Many argued that the east was still unsettled and that Han Xian and Yang Feng, arrogant with past service, could not be subdued in haste—zisui denotes wanton, raging insolence.

sentences.zh: 睢音火季反，又火佳反。

translations.literal: Sui is read huo-ji fan, also huo-jia fan.
translations.idiomatic: The character is read huo-ji or huo-jia.

sentences.zh: 《史記》：「盜跖日殺不辜，暴戾恣睢。」

translations.literal: The Records of the Grand Historian says: "Robber Zhi daily killed the innocent, cruel and overbearing."
translations.idiomatic: The Records says: "Robber Zhi daily killed the innocent, cruel and overbearing."

sentences.zh: 未可卒制。

translations.literal: It cannot be suddenly controlled.
translations.idiomatic: They could not be subdued in haste.

sentences.zh: 彧乃勸操曰：「昔晉文公納周襄王，而諸侯景從；

translations.literal: Xun Yu thereupon urged Cao Cao, saying: "Formerly Duke Wen of Jin received King Xiang of Zhou, and the feudal lords followed like shadows;
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu urged Cao Cao: "When Duke Wen of Jin received King Xiang of Zhou, the feudal lords flocked to him;

sentences.zh: 《左傳》，卜偃言於晉侯曰：「求諸侯莫如勤王，諸侯信之，且大義也。」

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary: Boyan said to the ruler of Jin, 'To seek the feudal lords there is nothing like serving the king— the feudal lords will trust it, and it is moreover the great righteousness.'
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary records Boyan telling the Jin ruler: 'To win the feudal lords, nothing surpasses serving the king— they will trust you, and it is the great righteous cause.'

sentences.zh: 晉侯以左師逆王，王入于王城，取太叔於溫，殺之於隰城，遂定霸業，天下服從也。

translations.literal: The ruler of Jin with the left army went to meet the king; the king entered Wangcheng, took the Grand Uncle at Wen, killed him at Yicheng, and thus settled the hegemony—all under Heaven submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's ruler met the king with the left army; the king entered Wangcheng, seized the Grand Uncle at Wen, executed him at Yicheng, and secured the hegemony until all under Heaven submitted.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖爲義帝縞素，而天下歸心。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor of Han wore mourning white for Emperor Yi, and all under Heaven turned their hearts to him.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor wore mourning for Emperor Yi and won the hearts of the realm.

sentences.zh: 項羽殺義帝於郴，高祖爲義帝發喪。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu killed Emperor Yi at Chen; the High Ancestor held mourning for Emperor Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang Yu killed Emperor Yi at Chen, the High Ancestor held mourning for him.

sentences.zh: 高祖大哭，發使告諸侯曰：「天下共立義帝，北面事之。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor wept greatly and sent envoys to tell the feudal lords: "All under Heaven jointly enthroned Emperor Yi, and we served him facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor wept and sent envoys to the feudal lords: "All under Heaven jointly enthroned Emperor Yi, and we served him as sovereign.

sentences.zh: 今項羽放殺義帝，大逆無道，寡人親爲發喪，兵皆縞素。」

translations.literal: Now Xiang Yu cast aside and killed Emperor Yi—great rebellion and devoid of the Way. I personally hold mourning; the troops all wear white mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Now Xiang Yu cast aside and murdered Emperor Yi—great treason. I personally hold mourning, and the troops all wear white."

sentences.zh: 自天子蒙塵，蒙，冒也。

translations.literal: Since the Son of Heaven suffered dust on the road—meng means to suffer.
translations.idiomatic: Since the emperor fell into exile—meng means to suffer hardship.

sentences.zh: 左傳臧文仲曰：「天子蒙塵於外，敢不奔問官守。」

translations.literal: Zang Wenzhong in the Zuo Commentary said: "The Son of Heaven suffers dust abroad—how dare we not rush to inquire after official duty?"
translations.idiomatic: Zang Wenzhong said in the Zuo Commentary: "When the Son of Heaven suffers exile abroad, who would not rush to serve?"

sentences.zh: 將軍首唱義兵，徒以山東擾亂，未遑遠赴，雖禦難於外，乃心無不在王室。

translations.literal: The General was first to raise the righteous army, but only because the east of the mountains was in turmoil had he no leisure to go far in haste; though defending against calamity abroad, his heart was never absent from the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: You were first to raise the righteous banner, but turmoil in the east kept you from going to his aid; though you fought enemies abroad, your heart never left the royal house.

sentences.zh: 《尚書》曰：「雖爾身在外，乃心無不在王室。」

translations.literal: The Documents says: "Though your person is abroad, your heart is never absent from the royal house."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says: "Though your body is abroad, your heart never leaves the royal house."

sentences.zh: 乃，汝也。

translations.literal: Nai means you.
translations.idiomatic: Nai means "you."

sentences.zh: 今鑾駕旋軫，鄭玄注《周禮》曰：「軫，輿後橫木也。」

translations.literal: Now the imperial carriage turns back its wheels—Zheng Xuan annotates the Rites of Zhou: "Zhen is the crossbeam behind the carriage."
translations.idiomatic: Now the imperial carriage is turning homeward—Zheng Xuan glosses zhen as the rear crossbeam of the carriage.

sentences.zh: 東京榛蕪，義士有存本之思，兆人懷感舊之哀。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital is overgrown with weeds; men of righteousness harbor thoughts of preserving the root; the myriad people cherish grief for the old.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang lies in ruins, loyal men yearn to restore the dynasty, and the people mourn the capital they have lost.

sentences.zh: 誠因此時奉主上以從人望，大順也；

translations.literal: Truly to take this moment, uphold the sovereign above to follow the people's hopes—this is the great accord;
translations.idiomatic: If you seize this moment to receive the emperor and satisfy the people's hopes, you will align with the greatest mandate;

sentences.zh: 秉至公以服天下，大略也；

translations.literal: to hold utmost fairness to bring all under Heaven to submission—this is the great strategy;
translations.idiomatic: hold yourself to utmost fairness and win the realm—that is the grand strategy;

sentences.zh: 扶弘義以致英俊，大德也。

translations.literal: to uphold expansive righteousness to draw men of excellence—this is the great virtue.
translations.idiomatic: and uphold righteous purpose to gather the talented—that is supreme virtue.

sentences.zh: 四方雖有逆節，其何能爲？

translations.literal: Though the four quarters have rebellious conduct, what can they accomplish?
translations.idiomatic: Rebels may stir in the provinces, but what can they achieve?

sentences.zh: 韓暹、楊奉，安足恤哉！

translations.literal: Han Xian and Yang Feng—how are they worth worrying over!
translations.idiomatic: Han Xian and Yang Feng are hardly worth your concern!

sentences.zh: 若不時定，使豪桀生心，後雖爲慮，亦無及矣。」

translations.literal: If you do not settle matters in timely fashion and let heroes and champions take heart, afterward even if you take thought, it will be too late."
translations.idiomatic: If you delay, ambitious rivals will take heart; even if you reconsider later, it will be too late."

sentences.zh: 操從之。

translations.literal: Cao Cao followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 及帝都許，以彧爲侍中，守尚書令。

translations.literal: When the emperor established the capital at Xu, Yu was made palace attendant, acting director of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved to Xu, Xun Yu became palace attendant and acting director of the secretariat,

sentences.zh: 操每征伐在外，其軍國之事，皆與彧籌焉。

translations.literal: Whenever Cao campaigned abroad, the military and state affairs, all were planned with Yu.
translations.idiomatic: and every military and civil matter while Cao campaigned was planned with him,

sentences.zh: 彧又進操計謀之士從子攸，

translations.literal: Yu further advanced to Cao planning strategists: his nephew You,
translations.idiomatic: He recommended his nephew Xun You,

sentences.zh: 〈魏志，荀攸字公達。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Records: Xun You courtesy name Gongda.
translations.idiomatic: 〈the Wei Records giving his style as Gongda,

sentences.zh: 太祖素聞攸名，與語大恱，謂彧曰：「公達非常人，吾得與計事，天下當何憂哉？」〉

translations.literal: Taizu long heard You's name; spoke with him and was greatly pleased; said to Yu: Gongda is no ordinary man—if I obtain to plan affairs with him, what should the realm worry?〉
translations.idiomatic: Taizu long heard You's name; spoke with him and was greatly pleased; said to Yu: "Gongda is no ordinary man—if I obtain to plan affairs with him, what should the realm worry?"〉

sentences.zh: 及鍾繇、郭嘉、

translations.literal: and Zhong Yao, Guo Jia,
translations.idiomatic: along with Zhong Yao, Guo Jia,

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Records: Jia courtesy name Fengxiao, a man of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Guo Jia of Yingchuan, styled Fengxiao,

sentences.zh: 戲志才，籌畫士也，太祖甚器之，早卒。

translations.literal: Xi Zhicai was a planning strategist; Taizu greatly esteemed him; died early.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zhicai, a brilliant planner whom Cao Cao prized, died young,

sentences.zh: 太祖與彧書曰：「自志才亡後，莫可與計事者。

translations.literal: Taizu wrote Yu a letter, saying: Since Zhicai died, none can plan affairs with me.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu wrote Yu a letter, saying: "Since Zhicai died, none can plan affairs with me.

sentences.zh: 汝、潁固多竒士，誰可以繼之？」

translations.literal: Ru and Ying surely have many strange gentlemen—who can succeed him?
translations.idiomatic: asking who among the Ruying scholars could replace him,"

sentences.zh: 彧薦嘉，召見論天下事，太祖曰：「使孤成大業者，必此人也。」〉

translations.literal: Yu recommended Jia; summoned audience to discuss realm affairs; Taizu said: He who makes orphan complete the great enterprise must be this man.〉
translations.idiomatic: Yu recommended Jia; summoned audience to discuss realm affairs; Taizu said: "He who makes orphan complete the great enterprise must be this man.〉"

translations.literal: Chen Qun, Du Xi,
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qun, Du Xi,

translations.idiomatic: 〈Du Xi, styled Zixu, from Yingchuan,

sentences.zh: 荀彧薦襲，太祖以爲丞相軍謀祭酒，魏國建，爲侍中。〉

translations.idiomatic: recommended by Xun Yu as army planning libationer and later palace attendant of Wei,〉

translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi,

translations.idiomatic: 〈styled Zhongda, the future Jin Xuandi,〉

translations.literal: Xi Zhicai and others—all praised his recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: and Xi Zhicai—every nomination won praise,

translations.idiomatic: only the appointments of Yan Xiang to Yang province

translations.literal: 〈The Sanfu Judgment Record says: Xiang courtesy name Wenze, a man of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: 〈failed: "the Sanfu Judgment Record names Yan Xiang of Jingzhao,

sentences.zh: 少聦博有膽智，爲楊州刺史。

translations.literal: In youth clever, broad, with courage and wisdom; became Yangzhou governor.
translations.idiomatic: clever and bold as governor of Yang,

sentences.zh: 後爲孫策廬江太守李術所殺。」〉

translations.literal: Later was killed by Sun Ce's Lujiang governor Li Shu.〉
translations.idiomatic: until Li Shu of Lujiang killed him for Sun Ce,"〉

sentences.zh: 韋康爲涼州，後並負敗焉。

translations.literal: Wei Kang as Liangzhou—afterward both met defeat.
translations.idiomatic: and Wei Kang to Liang province—both ended badly,

sentences.zh: 〈康字元將，京兆人。

translations.literal: 〈Kang courtesy name Yuanjiang, a man of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Wei Kang, styled Yuanjiang, from Jingzhao,

sentences.zh: 父端，從涼州牧徵爲太僕，康代爲涼州刺史，時人榮之。

translations.literal: Father Duan, following Liangzhou governor's summons became grand coachman; Kang replaced him as Liangzhou governor; people of the time honored it.
translations.idiomatic: succeeded his father Wei Duan as governor of Liang when the latter was summoned as grand coachman, an honor then much remarked,

sentences.zh: 後爲馬超所圍，堅守歷時，救軍不至，遂爲超所殺。〉

translations.literal: Later was besieged by Ma Chao, held firm for a long time, relief troops did not arrive, then was killed by Chao.〉
translations.idiomatic: until Ma Chao besieged him, relief never came, and Ma Chao killed him,〉

sentences.zh: 袁紹旣兼河朔之地，有驕氣。

translations.literal: After Yuan Shao had annexed the lands north of the River, he had arrogant air.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao grew arrogant after swallowing the north of the Yellow River,

translations.idiomatic: while Cao Cao had just been beaten by Zhang Xiu at Wancheng,

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Records: Zhang Xiu at Nanyang surrendered, then regretted it, and rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Zhang Xiu having surrendered at Nanyang then rebelled,

sentences.zh: 操與戰，軍敗爲流矢所中。〉

translations.literal: Cao fought him; the army was defeated and was struck by a stray arrow.〉
translations.idiomatic: and wounded Cao Cao with a stray arrow in the defeat,〉

sentences.zh: 紹與操書甚倨。

translations.literal: Shao's letter to Cao was very arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao's letter to him was insultingly arrogant,

sentences.zh: 〈 陳琳爲紹作檄書曰：「操祖父騰饕餮放橫，父嵩乞匄攜養，操贅閹遺醜。」

translations.literal: 〈Chen Lin for Shao made a proclamation saying: Cao's grandfather Teng was gluttonous and unrestrained; father Song begged and carried to raise him; Cao is a leftover eunuch's ugly remnant.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Chen Lin for Shao made a proclamation saying: "Cao's grandfather Teng was gluttonous and unrestrained; father Song begged and carried to raise him; Cao is a leftover eunuch's ugly remnant."

sentences.zh: 並倨慢之詞也。〉

translations.literal: All are arrogant and contemptuous words.〉
translations.idiomatic: all of it arrogant abuse,〉

sentences.zh: 操大怒，欲先攻之，而患力不敵，以謀於彧。

translations.literal: Cao was greatly angry, wished first to attack him, yet worried strength would not match, and consulted Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao raged and wished to strike Yuan Shao first but feared his strength and asked Xun Yu,

sentences.zh: 彧量紹雖強，終爲操所制，乃說先取呂布，然後圖紹，操從之。

translations.literal: Yu measured that though Shao was strong, in the end he would be controlled by Cao; then urged first to take Lü Bu, then plan Shao; Cao followed it.
translations.idiomatic: who judged that Yuan Shao could still be mastered but Lü Bu must be taken first; Cao Cao agreed,

sentences.zh: 三年，遂擒呂布，定徐州。

translations.literal: In the third year, then captured Lü Bu, settled Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: and in 198 CE captured Lü Bu and secured Xu province,

sentences.zh: 五年，袁紹率大衆以攻許，操與相距。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Yuan Shao led a great host to attack Xu; Cao opposed him at distance.
translations.idiomatic: In 200 CE Yuan Shao marched on Xu while Cao Cao held the line,

sentences.zh: 紹甲兵甚盛，議者咸懷惶懼。

translations.literal: Shao's armor and weapons were very strong; discussers all harbored panic and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao's host was overwhelming and many advisers panicked,

sentences.zh: 少府孔融謂彧曰：「袁紹地廣兵彊，田豐、許攸智計之士爲其謀，

translations.literal: Minister of the lesser treasury Kong Rong said to Yu: Yuan Shao's territory is broad and troops strong; Tian Feng, Xu You—men of wisdom and plan—are his strategists,
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the lesser treasury Kong Rong said to Yu: "Yuan Shao's territory is broad and troops strong; Tian Feng, Xu You—men of wisdom and plan—are his strategists,

sentences.zh: 〈《先賢行狀》：「豐字元皓，鉅鹿人。

translations.literal: 〈The Exemplary Conduct of Former Worthies: Feng courtesy name Yuanhao, a man of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: 〈the Exemplary Conduct calls Tian Feng Yuanhao of Julu,

sentences.zh: 天姿瓌傑，權略多竒。」

translations.literal: Heaven's gifts grand and outstanding, stratagem and plan many strange.
translations.idiomatic: gifted and full of stratagems,

translations.literal: Xu You courtesy name Ziyuan.〉
translations.idiomatic: Xu You being styled Ziyuan,〉

translations.literal: Shen Pei, Feng Ji—utterly loyal ministers attend their tasks,
translations.idiomatic: while Shen Pei and Feng Ji were loyal ministers handling affairs,

sentences.zh: 〈配字正南，魏郡人。

translations.literal: 〈Pei courtesy name Zhengnan, a man of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Shen Pei, styled Zhengnan, from Wei commandery,

sentences.zh: 忠烈慷慨，有不可犯之色。

translations.literal: Loyal and ardent, generous and bold, having an unassailable bearing.
translations.idiomatic: fiercely loyal and formidable in manner,

sentences.zh: 紹領兾州，委配腹心之任。

translations.literal: Shao led Ji Province, entrusted Pei with heart-and-belly duty.
translations.idiomatic: and Yuan Shao, as governor of Ji, had entrusted Shen Pei with his closest counsels.

sentences.zh: 《英雄記》曰：「紀字元圖。

translations.literal: The Record of Heroes says: Ji courtesy name Yuantu.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes gives Feng Ji courtesy name Yuantu,

sentences.zh: 初，紹去董卓，與許攸及紀俱詣兾州，紹以紀聦達有計策，甚信之。」〉

sentences.zh: 〈《左傳》曰：「聖達節，次守節。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The Zuo Tradition says: Sages comprehend the season; next guard the season.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Zuo Tradition says: "Sages comprehend the season; next guard the season.〉"

sentences.zh: 於是增封千戶，并前二千戶。

translations.literal: Thereupon added enfeoffment one thousand households, together with before two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: so his fief rose by a thousand households to two thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 又欲授以正司，

translations.literal: Again wished to confer on him the regular office,
translations.idiomatic: The court again meant to give him a formal appointment to the post,

sentences.zh: 〈彧先守尚書令，今欲正除也。〉

translations.literal: Note: Yu had first been acting guardian director of the secretariat; now they wished to appoint him to the substantive post.〉
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Xun Yu had been serving as acting director of the secretariat; the plan was now to confirm him in the full title.〉

sentences.zh: 彧使荀攸深自陳讓，至于十數，乃止。

translations.literal: Yu had Xun You press his declinations earnestly, reaching to a dozen or more times, and then it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu sent Xun You to press his repeated refusals—more than ten times—before the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 操將伐劉表，問彧所策。

translations.literal: Cao was about to attack Liu Biao and asked Yu what strategy to take.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao was preparing to strike Liu Biao, he asked Xun Yu for a plan.

sentences.zh: 彧曰：「今華夏以平，荊、漢知亡矣，可聲出宛、葉而閒行輕進，以掩其不意。」

translations.literal: Yu said: Now the central lands are already pacified; Jing and the Han region know they are doomed. You may make a show of marching out through Wan and Ye while sending a light column by secret routes to strike where they do not expect.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu said, “The heartland is already settled; the Jing–Han region knows it is finished. Feint a thrust through Wan and Ye, then slip a fast, light force along byways to catch them off guard.”

sentences.zh: 操從之。

translations.literal: Cao followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao adopted the advice.

sentences.zh: 會表病死。

translations.literal: It happened that Biao fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao then fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏志》，操如彧計，表子琮以州逆降。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Records states: Cao followed Yu’s plan, and Biao’s son Cong surrendered the province in submission.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei Records notes that Cao Cao followed Xun Yu’s design and that Liu Biao’s son Liu Cong yielded the province in surrender.〉

sentences.zh: 十七年，董昭等

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Dong Zhao and others
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of the Jian’an era, Dong Zhao and others

sentences.zh: 〈昭字公仁，濟陰人也。〉

translations.literal: Note: Zhao, courtesy name Gongren, was a man of Jiyin.〉
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Dong Zhao, styled Gongren, came from Jiyin.〉

sentences.zh: 欲共進操爵國公，九錫備物，

translations.literal: wished jointly to advance Cao’s noble rank to duke of a state and to complete the nine bestowals and their full paraphernalia,
translations.idiomatic: They sought jointly to raise Cao Cao to the rank of duke of a state and to award him the full regalia of the nine bestowals,

sentences.zh: 〈禮含文嘉曰：「九錫一曰車馬，二曰衣服，三曰樂器，四曰朱戶，五曰納陛，六曰虎賁百人，七曰斧鉞，八曰弓矢，九曰秬鬯，謂之九錫。

translations.literal: 〈The Rites, Hanwenjia chapter, says: The nine bestowals are, first, chariots and horses; second, robes; third, musical instruments; fourth, vermilion doors; fifth, the stepped ascent; sixth, a hundred tiger guards; seventh, axe and halberd; eighth, bow and arrows; ninth, black millet ale—these are called the nine bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The ritual text Hanwenjia lists the nine bestowals: "chariots and horses; robes; instruments; vermilion doors; the palace stair; a hundred tiger guards; the axe and halberd; bow and arrows; and the dark-millet ale—the nine gifts so named.

sentences.zh: 錫，與也，九錫皆如其德。」

translations.literal: Xi means ‘to give’; each of the nine bestowals matches his virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Xi means "to grant," and each of the nine honors was meant to match the recipient's virtue."

sentences.zh: 《左傳》曰：「分魯公以大路大旂，夏后氏之璜，封父之繁弱，祝宗卜史，備物典策。」〉

translations.literal: The Zuo Tradition says: "They divided to the duke of Lu the great chariot and great banner, the Xia hou's jade, Fengfu's bow, invocators, lineage masters, diviners, and scribes—complete paraphernalia and canonical documents." Closing note.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Tradition says: "They divided to the duke of Lu the great chariot and great banner, the Xia hou's jade, Fengfu's bow, invocators, lineage masters, diviners, and scribes—complete paraphernalia and canonical documents." Closing note.〉

sentences.zh: 密以訪彧。

translations.literal: Secretly consulted Yu about it.
translations.idiomatic: They sounded Xun Yu out on the plan in private.

sentences.zh: 彧曰「曹公本興義兵，以匡振漢朝，雖勳庸崇著，猶秉忠貞之節。

translations.literal: Yu said: Lord Cao originally raised a righteous host to rescue and restore the Han house; though his merit and achievements tower high, he still holds to loyal and steadfast integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu said, “Lord Cao first took up arms in a righteous cause to set the Han to rights. However great his merit, he has kept faith with the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 君子愛人以德，不宜如此。」

translations.literal: A gentleman loves others by nurturing their virtue; it is not fitting to do thus.
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman serves another’s good by moral means; this is not the way to treat him.”

sentences.zh: 事遂寑。

translations.literal: The matter then was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 〈《禮記》曰「君子之愛人也以德，細人之愛人也以姑息」也。〉

translations.literal: The Record of Rites says: "The gentleman's love for others is by virtue; the petty man's love for others is by indulgence." Closing note.〉
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The Record of Rites says: "The gentleman's love for others is by virtue; the petty man's love for others is by indulgence." Closing note.〉

sentences.zh: 操心不能平。

translations.literal: Cao’s heart could not be calmed.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao could not set the slight aside.

sentences.zh: 會南征孫權，表請彧勞軍于譙，因表留彧曰：「臣聞古之遣將，上設監督之重，下建副二之任，

translations.literal: When he was about to campaign south against Sun Quan, he memorialized asking Yu to review the army at Qiao, and by memorial sought to detain Yu, saying: I have heard that in antiquity when sending forth generals, above they set the weight of overseers; below they established the duty of seconds,
translations.idiomatic: On the southern expedition against Sun Quan, Cao Cao memorialized that Xun Yu should review the troops at Qiao, then used a second memorial to keep him there: “Ancient custom placed heavy overseers above a field commander and paired seconds below him,

sentences.zh: 〈《史記》，齊景公以田穰苴爲將軍，扞燕。

translations.literal: 〈The Records states: Duke Jing of Qi made Tian Rangju general to resist Yan.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Records tells how Duke Jing of Qi named Tian Rangju general against Yan.

sentences.zh: 苴曰：「臣素卑賤，擢之閭伍之中，加之大夫之上，士卒未附，百姓不信，權輕，願得君之寵臣，國之所尊，以監軍，乃可。」

translations.literal: Rangju said: I have always been base and lowly; raised from the lanes and squads and set above great officers, the troops are not yet attached and the people do not trust me; my authority is light. I wish to obtain one of your favored ministers, whom the state esteems, to oversee the army—only then may it be done.
translations.idiomatic: Rangju replied, “I am of mean origin, pulled from the ranks above senior officers; the soldiers do not yet follow me, and the people do not trust my light authority. Give me one of your trusted ministers, honored in the state, to supervise the host, and it can be done.”

sentences.zh: 景公許之，使莊賈往。

translations.literal: Duke Jing granted it and sent Zhuang Jia to go.
translations.idiomatic: The duke agreed and sent Zhuang Jia.

sentences.zh: 即監督之義也。〉

translations.literal: This is the meaning of overseer. Closing note.〉
translations.idiomatic: That is the sense of “overseer” intended here. End of gloss.〉

sentences.zh: 所以尊嚴國命，謀而鮮過者也。

translations.literal: by which the dignity of the state’s command is upheld and plans seldom go wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the majesty of the state’s orders is upheld and counsel rarely errs.

sentences.zh: 〈《左傳》曰：「謀而鮮過，惠訓不倦。」〉

translations.literal: The Zuo Tradition says: In planning seldom erring, in kindly instruction never weary.〉
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The Zuo Tradition praises counsel that seldom fails and teaching that never tires.〉

sentences.zh: 臣今當濟江，奉辭伐罪，宜有大使肅將王命。

translations.literal: Your servant now must cross the Yangzi, bearing the charge to punish the guilty; there ought to be a great envoy solemnly bearing the king’s command.
translations.idiomatic: I am about to cross the river on a punitive mission; a senior envoy should carry the imperial charge with fitting gravity.

sentences.zh: 文武並用，自古有之。

translations.literal: Civil and military used together—since antiquity there has been this.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military means have always been paired.

sentences.zh: 使持節侍中守尚書令萬歲亭侯彧，國之望臣，德洽華夏，旣停軍所次，便宜與臣俱進，宣示國命，威懷醜虜。

translations.literal: The commissioner bearing credentials, palace attendant, acting guardian director of the secretariat, Marquis of Wansui Precinct, Yu, is a minister on whom the state’s hopes rest; his virtue spreads through the central lands. Since he has halted where the army camps, it is fitting that he advance together with your servant, proclaiming the state’s command and overawing and winning the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner with insignia, palace attendant, acting director of the secretariat, and Marquis of Wansui Precinct, Xun Yu, is a pillar of the state whose virtue runs through the realm. As he has paused where the army rests, he should march with me to proclaim the court’s will and overawe the foe.

sentences.zh: 軍禮尚速，不及先請，臣輒留彧，依以爲重。」

translations.literal: Military ritual esteems speed; there was no time to request beforehand; your servant therefore detained Yu, relying on him for weight.
translations.idiomatic: Field etiquette prizes speed, so I could not wait for prior approval; I have therefore kept Xun Yu with the army as my mainstay.”

sentences.zh: 書奏，帝從之，遂以彧爲侍中、光祿大夫，持節，參丞相軍事。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, the emperor followed it, and Yu was then made palace attendant, grand master of splendid happiness, bearer of credentials, and participant in the chancellor’s military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the memorial, and Xun Yu was appointed palace attendant, grand master of splendid happiness, credential-bearer, and adviser on the chancellor’s staff.

sentences.zh: 至濡須，

translations.literal: When they reached Ruxu,
translations.idiomatic: When the host reached Ruxu,

sentences.zh: 〈濡須，水名也，在今和州歷陽縣西南。

translations.literal: Note: Ruxu is the name of a water, now southwest of Liyang County in Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Ruxu is a river name, southwest of present-day Liyang in Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 吳錄曰：「孫權聞操來，夾水立塢，狀如偃月，以相拒，月餘乃退。」〉

translations.literal: The Wu Record says: When Sun Quan heard Cao was coming, he built stockades along both banks in the shape of a reclining moon to oppose him; after more than a month Cao withdrew. Closing note.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Record says: "When Sun Quan heard Cao was coming, he built stockades along both banks in the shape of a reclining moon to oppose him; after more than a month Cao withdrew. Closing note.〉"

sentences.zh: 彧病留壽春，

translations.literal: Yu fell ill and remained at Shouchun,
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu fell ill and was left at Shouchun,

sentences.zh: 〈壽春，縣，屬淮南郡，今壽州郡也。〉

translations.literal: Note: Shouchun is a county belonging to Huainan commandery; it is now Shouzhou commandery.〉
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Shouchun county lay in Huainan commandery, in what is now Shouzhou.〉

sentences.zh: 操饋之食，發視，乃空器也，於是飲藥而卒。

translations.literal: Cao sent him food; when he opened and looked, it was an empty vessel; thereupon he drank poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent a meal; when the cover was lifted, the vessels were empty. Xun Yu took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 時年五十。

translations.literal: At the time he was fifty sui.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty years old.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝春秋》，董承之誅，伏后與父完書，言司空殺董承，帝方爲報怨。

translations.literal: 〈The Annals of Emperor Xian: At Dong Cheng’s execution, Empress Fu wrote to her father Wan, saying the minister of works had killed Dong Cheng and the emperor was then seeking revenge.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Annals of Emperor Xian relates that after Dong Cheng’s death, Empress Fu wrote her father Fu Wan that the minister of works had executed Dong Cheng while the emperor still nursed a grievance.

sentences.zh: 完得書以示彧，彧惡之，隱而不言。

translations.literal: When Wan received the letter he showed it to Yu; Yu detested it and concealed it without speaking.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Wan showed the letter to Xun Yu, who was appalled and kept silent.

sentences.zh: 完以示其妻弟樊普，普封以呈太祖，太祖陰爲之備。

translations.literal: Wan showed it to his wife’s younger brother Fan Pu; Pu sealed and presented it to the Grand Progenitor, who secretly made preparations on account of it.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Wan also showed it to his brother-in-law Fan Pu, who sealed it and sent it to Cao Cao, who quietly laid his plans.

sentences.zh: 彧恐事覺，欲自發之，因求使至鄴，勸太祖以女配帝。

translations.literal: Yu feared the affair would be discovered and wished to expose it himself; therefore he sought mission to Ye and urged the Grand Progenitor to give a daughter to the emperor as consort.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing exposure, Xun Yu tried to get ahead of the plot by asking leave to go to Ye and urging Cao Cao to marry a daughter into the palace.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「今朝廷有伏后，吾女何得配上？」

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: Now the court has Empress Fu; how could my daughter be matched to the throne?
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao replied, “The court already has Empress Fu; how can my daughter enter the harem?”

sentences.zh: 彧曰：「伏后無子，性又凶邪，往甞與父書，言詞醜惡，可因此廢也。」

translations.literal: Yu said: Empress Fu has no sons; her nature is moreover cruel and depraved; in the past she once wrote her father with ugly words—on this ground she may be deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu said, “The empress is sonless and vicious; she once wrote her father intemperate letters—grounds enough to set her aside.”

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「卿昔何不道之？」

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: Why did you not speak of it in the past?
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao asked, “Why did you never mention this before?”

sentences.zh: 彧陽驚曰：「昔已甞爲公言也。」

translations.literal: Yu feigned surprise and said: In the past I already once spoke to the lord about it.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu pretended astonishment: “I did tell you, my lord.”

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「此豈小事，而吾忘之！」

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: How could this be a small matter, and I forget it!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, “A matter of this weight—and I would forget?”

sentences.zh: 太祖以此恨彧，而外含容之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor on this account harbored resentment toward Yu, yet outwardly contained him.
translations.idiomatic: From that day Cao Cao nursed a grudge against Xun Yu while still treating him with outward respect.

sentences.zh: 至董昭建魏公議，彧意不同，欲言之於太祖，乃齎璽書犒軍，飲饗禮畢，彧請間，太祖知彧欲言，揖而遣之，遂不得。

translations.literal: When Dong Zhao raised the proposal for the Wei duke, Yu’s mind differed; he wished to speak of it to the Grand Progenitor. Then bearing the imperial document he went to reward the army; when the drinking feast rites were finished, Yu asked for a private audience; the Grand Progenitor knew Yu wished to speak, bowed with hands joined and sent him away, so he could not get through.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhao pressed the motion to ennoble Cao as duke of Wei, Xun Yu disagreed and meant to remonstrate. He carried an edict to feast the army; after the banquet he asked for a private word. Cao Cao guessed his intent, bowed him out, and gave him no chance to speak.

sentences.zh: 留之，卒於壽春。〉

translations.literal: Detained him; he died at Shouchun. Closing note.〉
translations.idiomatic: He was kept there and died at Shouchun. End of gloss.〉

sentences.zh: 帝哀惜之，祖日爲之廢讌樂。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned and pitied him; on the ancestral day for him he suspended feasting and music.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved for him and canceled banquet music on the ancestral day observed in his honor.

sentences.zh: 〈祖日謂祭祖神之日，因爲讌樂也。

translations.literal: Note: Ancestral day means the day of sacrificing to the ancestral spirit; on it there was feasting and music.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: “Ancestral day” was the feast honoring the patron spirit of travel,

sentences.zh: 《風俗通》曰：「共工氏子曰脩，好遠遊，祀以爲祖神。

translations.literal: The Comprehensive Meaning of Customs and Usages says: "Gonggong's son was named Xiu; he loved to travel far and was sacrificed to as the ancestral spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The Comprehensive Meaning of Customs says: "Gonggong's son was named Xiu; he loved to travel far and was sacrificed to as the ancestral spirit.

sentences.zh: 漢以午日祖。」〉

translations.literal: The Han took the wu day for the ancestral rite." Closing note.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Han marked that rite on the wu day of the cycle." End of gloss.〉

sentences.zh: 謚曰敬侯。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was reverent marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Reverent Marquis.

sentences.zh: 明年，操遂稱魏公云。

translations.literal: The next year, Cao then styled himself duke of Wei, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Cao Cao took the title duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自遷帝西京，山東騰沸，

translations.literal: Discussion says: From the time the emperor was moved to the western capital, east of the mountains boiled up,
translations.idiomatic: The historian’s judgment: After the emperor was removed to the western capital, the lands east of the mountains seethed,

sentences.zh: 〈詩曰：「百川沸騰。」〉

translations.literal: The Odes says: The hundred streams boil up.〉
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The Odes speaks of “the hundred streams boiling over.”〉

sentences.zh: 天下之命倒縣矣。

translations.literal: The fate of the realm hung inverted.
translations.idiomatic: the fate of the empire hung upside down.

sentences.zh: 〈趙岐注《孟子》曰：「倒縣猶困苦也。」〉

translations.literal: Zhao Qi’s commentary on Mencius says: Inverted hanging is like extreme hardship.〉
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Zhao Qi glosses “inverted” as utter distress.〉

sentences.zh: 荀君乃越河、兾，間關以從曹氏。

translations.literal: Lord Xun then crossed the Yellow River and Ji, in hardship and twists to follow the Cao house.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Xun Yu crossed the Yellow River and the Ji region, making a hard road of it to join the Caos.

sentences.zh: 〈間關猶展轉也。〉

translations.literal: Note: Jianguan is like turning and tossing.〉
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: “Jianguan” here means a winding, difficult journey.〉

sentences.zh: 察其定舉措，

translations.literal: Observing his settled measures,
translations.idiomatic: Watching how he set policy,

sentences.zh: 〈措，置也。〉

translations.literal: Note: Cuo means to place.〉
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Cuo means “to set” or “to arrange.”〉

sentences.zh: 立言策，崇明王略，以急國艱，豈云因亂假義，以就違正之謀乎？

translations.literal: establishing words and plans, exalting and clarifying the kingly strategy, to relieve the state’s peril—how could one say he borrowed righteousness amid chaos to pursue a design that violated the right?
translations.idiomatic: framing counsel and exalting the royal design to ease the dynasty’s peril—can that be dismissed as seizing a moral pretext in turmoil to serve a crooked end?

sentences.zh: 〈言彧本心不背漢也，〉

translations.literal: Note: This says Yu’s original mind did not turn against the Han.〉
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The point is that Xun Yu’s heart never turned against the Han.〉

sentences.zh: 誠仁爲己任，期紓民於倉卒也。

translations.literal: Truly he took benevolence as his burden, hoping to relieve the people in sudden crisis.
translations.idiomatic: He truly took humanity as his charge and hoped to spare the people in the crisis of the moment.

sentences.zh: 〈紓，緩也，音舒。〉

translations.literal: Note: Shu means to ease; pronounced like shu.〉
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Shu means “to ease,” read like the character for “relax.”〉

sentences.zh: 及阻董昭之議，以致非命，豈數也夫！

translations.literal: When he blocked Dong Zhao’s proposal and thereby met an unnatural death—was it fate indeed!
translations.idiomatic: When he blocked Dong Zhao’s scheme and paid with his life, was that mere chance?

sentences.zh: 世言荀君者，通塞或過矣。

translations.literal: What the age says of Lord Xun, on success and obstruction, may sometimes go too far.
translations.idiomatic: Popular talk about Lord Xun Yu—whether he flourished or was blocked—often misses the mark.

sentences.zh: 常以爲中賢以下，道無求備，智筭有所研踈，原始未必要末。

translations.literal: I have always held that below middling worthies one does not demand completeness in the Way; in calculation of wisdom there are places refined or rough; tracing the beginning does not always require matching the end.
translations.idiomatic: Below the middling sage one cannot demand perfection: wit may excel in one place and falter in another, and a noble start need not guarantee the same end.

sentences.zh: 斯理之不可全詰者也。

translations.literal: This is a principle that cannot be exhaustively pressed.
translations.idiomatic: That is a truth no moral audit can exhaust.

sentences.zh: 夫以衞賜之賢，一說而斃兩國。

translations.literal: Now as for the worth of Wei Ci, with one persuasion he brought down two states.
translations.idiomatic: Even Wei Ci’s genius—one round of diplomacy undid two kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 〈兩國謂齊與吳也。

translations.literal: Note: The two states mean Qi and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The two states are Qi and Wu.

sentences.zh: 端木賜字子貢，衞人也。

translations.literal: Duanmu Ci, courtesy name Zigong, was a man of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Duanmu Ci, styled Zigong, was a native of Wei.

sentences.zh: 田常欲伐魯，仲尼令出使勸田常伐吳，常許之。

translations.literal: Tian Chang wished to attack Lu; Zhongni ordered him to go on mission and urge Tian Chang to attack Wu; Chang assented.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Chang planned to attack Lu, Confucius sent Zigong to persuade him to strike Wu instead, and Tian Chang agreed.

sentences.zh: 賜又至吳，請夫差伐齊。

translations.literal: Ci also went to Wu and asked Fuchai to attack Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong then went to Wu and urged King Fuchai to march against Qi.

sentences.zh: 又之越，說句踐將兵助吳。

translations.literal: Again he went to Yue and persuaded Gou Jian to lead troops to aid Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He next visited Yue and talked Gou Jian into sending troops to help Wu.

sentences.zh: 又之晉，說以兵待吳伐齊之弊。

translations.literal: Again he went to Jin and persuaded them with troops to await the exhaustion of Wu’s attack on Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Jin and urged it to hold its army ready for the weariness that would follow Wu’s campaign in Qi.

sentences.zh: 吳旣勝齊，與晉爭彊，晉果敗吳，越襲其後，遂殺夫差。

translations.literal: Once Wu had defeated Qi, it contended with Jin for supremacy; Jin indeed defeated Wu, Yue struck from behind, and thereupon killed Fuchai.
translations.idiomatic: Wu beat Qi, then clashed with Jin for dominance; Jin broke Wu’s power, Yue struck from the rear, and Fuchai died.

sentences.zh: 故子貢一出，存魯，亂齊，破吳，彊晉，霸越。〉

translations.literal: Therefore one outing of Zigong preserved Lu, threw Qi into turmoil, broke Wu, strengthened Jin, and made Yue hegemon. Closing note.〉
translations.idiomatic: Thus a single mission preserved Lu, ruined Qi, shattered Wu, bolstered Jin, and crowned Yue. End of gloss.〉

sentences.zh: 彼非薄於仁而欲之，蓋有全必有喪也，斯又功之不兼者也。

translations.literal: It was not that he was shallow in benevolence yet desired it—where there is preservation there must also be loss; this again is where achievements cannot be combined.
translations.idiomatic: That was not because he scanted humanity for gain: every gain costs something else—no single deed can compass every good.

sentences.zh: 〈子貢不欲違仁義而致晉，但其事不兼濟也。

translations.literal: Note: Zigong did not wish to violate benevolence and rightness to bring about Jin, but the affair could not aid all sides.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Zigong did not mean to betray moral duty to elevate Jin, yet one stroke could not save every state.

sentences.zh: 言彧豈願彊曹氏令代漢哉？

translations.literal: This says how could Yu have wished to strengthen the Cao house to replace the Han?
translations.idiomatic: The text asks whether Xun Yu truly wanted to build the Caos into usurpers of the Han.

sentences.zh: 事不得已也。〉

translations.literal: The affair was what could not be helped. Closing note.〉
translations.idiomatic: He was caught in what could not be helped. End of gloss.〉

sentences.zh: 方時運之屯邅，

translations.literal: When the times’ fortune was blocked and halting,
translations.idiomatic: In an age stumbling through hardship,

sentences.zh: 〈《易》曰：「屯如邅如。」

translations.literal: The Changes says: Blocked like, halting like.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The Changes reads, “Blocked and stumbling,”

sentences.zh: 邅音竹連反。〉

translations.literal: Zhan is pronounced like zhu-lian fan. Closing note.〉
translations.idiomatic: with zhan read in the zhu-lian cut. End of gloss.〉

sentences.zh: 非雄才無以濟其溺，功高埶彊，則皇器自移矣。

translations.literal: Without heroic talent there is no way to save them from drowning; when merit is high and power strong, then the imperial regalia shifts of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Only a heroic talent could pull the realm from the flood; once power towers, the throne slips away on its own.

sentences.zh: 〈謂魏太祖功業大而神器自歸也。〉

translations.literal: Note: This means Wei’s Grand Progenitor’s achievements were great and the sacred vessel returned to him of itself.〉
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Cao Cao’s deeds grew so great that the mandate gravitated to him.〉

sentences.zh: 此又時之不可並也。

translations.literal: This again is where the times cannot be combined.
translations.idiomatic: That, too, is what the age will not allow to be reconciled.

sentences.zh: 蓋取其歸正而已，亦殺身以成仁之義也。

translations.literal: In general he took returning to the right as enough—it is also the meaning of destroying the body to complete benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: He chose to stand by the right even at the cost of his life—the sense of Confucius’s “die to perfect benevolence.”

translations.literal: Praise section marker.
translations.idiomatic: Section heading: encomium.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：公業稱豪，駿聲升騰。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Gongye was hailed a champion; his splendid name rose aloft.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium runs: Gongye was hailed a hero, and his fair fame climbed high.

sentences.zh: 權詭時偪，

translations.literal: He wielded stratagem when the times pressed,
translations.idiomatic: When crisis pressed, he answered with wiles,

sentences.zh: 〈謂詭辭以對卓。〉

translations.literal: Note: This means he used deceitful words to answer Dong Zhuo.〉
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: He dissembled before Dong Zhuo.〉

sentences.zh: 揮金僚朋。

translations.literal: scattering gold among colleagues and friends.
translations.idiomatic: He scattered gold among friends and allies.

sentences.zh: 〈揮，散也。〉

translations.literal: Note: Hui means to scatter.〉
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: “Scatter” is the sense of hui here.〉

sentences.zh: 北海天逸，音情頓挫。

translations.literal: The lord of Beihai was free as heaven; his tones and feeling rose and fell.
translations.idiomatic: The lord of Beihai moved with heaven’s ease, his voice and passion breaking in waves.

sentences.zh: 〈逸，縱也。

translations.literal: Note: Yi means to give free rein.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Here yi means “unrestrained ease.”

sentences.zh: 頓挫猶抑揚也。〉

translations.literal: Duncuo is like rising and falling. Closing note.〉
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Duncuo means cadence, rise and fall. End of gloss.〉

sentences.zh: 越俗易驚，孤音少和。

translations.literal: Yue customs are easily startled; a lone note seldom finds harmony.
translations.idiomatic: The south startles easily; a solitary voice rarely finds a chorus.

sentences.zh: 直轡安歸，高謀誰佐？

translations.literal: Straight reins—where to return? Lofty plans—who will assist?
translations.idiomatic: The straight road offers no homecoming; whose hand steadies so high a design?

sentences.zh: 〈直轡，直道也。

translations.literal: Note: Straight reins means the straight path.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: “Straight reins” stands for the upright way.

sentences.zh: 言其道無所歸，謀謨之高欲誰佐也。〉

translations.literal: It says his way had nowhere to return, and who would second so lofty a design. Closing note.〉
translations.idiomatic: It means he had no safe road back, and no ally for his grand counsel. End of gloss.〉

sentences.zh: 彧之有弼，誠感國疾。

translations.literal: In Yu’s having a helper, truly he felt the state’s sickness.
translations.idiomatic: That Xun Yu had a counterpart shows how keenly he felt the dynasty’s ailment.

sentences.zh: 功申運改，迹疑心一。

translations.literal: Merit extended, fortune changed; tracks seemed doubtful, yet the heart was one.
translations.idiomatic: Times shifted and deeds ran on; the record looks tangled, but the purpose never wavered.

sentences.zh: 〈迹若可疑，心如一心。〉

translations.literal: Note: The tracks seem doubtful, yet the heart is single-minded. Closing note.〉
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Outward signs may puzzle, inward resolve did not. End of gloss.〉
